text: for `K/ℚ` finite Galois the inertia subgroups of the primes of `𝓞 K` generate `Gal(K/ℚ)`, since their fixed field would otherwise be an everywhere-unramified extension of `ℚ`, which Minkowski's discriminant bound forbids; the recorded consequence is the genus-theory step that an abelian extension of a number field unramified at all finite places has Galois group of exponent dividing the base degree (Serre, *Topics in Galois Theory*, §4.4).

name: Locally flat embeddings of codimension one are locally bicollared
text: a locally flat embedded `(n−1)`-manifold in an `n`-manifold has two-sided product neighbourhoods locally, with the converse over domains charted on the model space; the local half of Brown's collaring theorem, whose global statement is a separate later target (M. Brown, *Ann. of Math.* 75 (1962)).

name: The places of the rational function field, classified
text: the places of `k(x)` are exactly the monic irreducible polynomials together with the place at infinity, with residue field `k[X]/(q)` and degree `deg q` at the finite place of `q` and degree one at infinity, so the degree-one places are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`; built on Mathlib's Ostrowski-type classification of the valuations of `k(X)` (Stichtenoth, Prop. 1.2.1 and Thm. 1.2.2).

name: The coding representation of an exchangeable sequence
text: jointly with its directing measure, an exchangeable sequence in a standard Borel space is the coordinatewise image of an i.i.d. uniform sequence under one fixed measurable map, the same map for every process, and conversely every such coded law is exchangeable — upgrading the conditional-law form of de Finetti announced earlier to a functional representation (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Prop. 1.4).

name: Mixed Hodge structures
text: a rational weight filtration together with a Hodge filtration on the complexification whose weight-graded pieces carry pure Hodge structures, with the comparison `ℂ ⊗ grᵂ_k ≅ (W_k)_ℂ/(W_{k−1})_ℂ` proved, pure structures embedded as one-weight mixed ones, and the Tate structure as the first example; Deligne's `I^{p,q}` bigrading and strictness are later targets (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*; Peters–Steenbrink).

name: The Artin–Tits group of a Coxeter matrix, and the braid group
text: the group presented by the braid-word relations of a Coxeter matrix, with its universal property and canonical surjection onto the Coxeter group, and its type-A instance the braid group on `n` strands, mapping onto `Sₙ` with the pure braid group as kernel and nonabelian from three strands on; braid groups are also being formalised upstream in mathlib4#32941 (Brieskorn–Saito; Birman).

name: The Verma module
text: `M(λ)`, the quotient of `U(L)` by the left ideal generated by the kernel of the Borel character, with its universal property: every highest weight module of weight `λ` is a quotient of `M(λ)`, and `M(λ)` has a unique irreducible quotient `L(λ)`; nonvanishing of `M(λ)` is pinned to the linear-independence half of PBW, still open, and is proved for `λ = 0` (Humphreys, §20).

name: The error function
text: `erf` and `erfc` with oddness, strict monotonicity, the limits at both infinities and the derivative, giving the Gaussian cumulative distribution function in closed form, `cdf = (1 + erf((x − m)/√(2v)))/2`; the declarations follow the shapes of the open mathlib4#34053 so they can be swapped out when it lands (DLMF, Ch. 7).

name: The Sard–Smale theorem
text: the critical values of a C^k Fredholm map from an open subset of a second-countable Banach space to a complete normed space are meagre, so its regular values are residual and dense; at the threshold k ≥ (dim ker)² + 1, not yet Smale's sharp k > index (Smale, Amer. J. Math. 87 (1965)).

name: The Nagell–Lutz theorem
text: for A, B ∈ ℤ, a nonzero rational torsion point on y² = x³ + Ax + B has integer coordinates with y = 0 or y² ∣ Δ (Silverman, AEC VIII.7.1); the long-model form over the fraction field of any UFD — integral except at order two, where 4x, 8y are integral, with ψ₂² ∣ 4Δ — is TauCeti#4348 and TauCeti#4358.

name: The Temperley–Lieb algebra and the Jones representation of the braid group
text: TL_n(R, δ) by generators e₁, …, e_{n−1} and its three relations, shown not to collapse, and σᵢ ↦ a·1 + a⁻¹eᵢ at δ = −(a² + a⁻²), satisfying the braid relations and giving a nontrivial B_n → TL_n(R, δ)ˣ (Jones, Bull. AMS 12 (1985)); the Markov trace, hence the Jones polynomial, is not yet built.

name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem in finite-difference form
text: a function on [0, ∞) right-continuous at 0 whose mixed forward differences with nonnegative steps satisfy (−1)ⁿ Δ_{h₁}⋯Δ_{hₙ} f ≥ 0 is the Laplace transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0, and conversely, so Hausdorff's difference condition is equivalent to the smooth complete monotonicity of TauCeti#2174 (Widder, *The Laplace Transform*, Ch. IV).

name: Every Brauer class contains a unique division algebra
text: each class in Br(K) is represented by a finite-dimensional central division K-algebra, unique up to K-algebra isomorphism (Gille–Szamuely §2.4), and the kernel of Br(K) → Br(L) is exactly the classes split by L (TauCeti#4210).

name: Polarizable rational Hodge structures are semisimple
text: every rational Hodge substructure of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has an orthogonal complement for the polarizing form which is again a rational Hodge substructure and complements it over ℚ and over ℂ (Peters–Steenbrink, *Mixed Hodge Structures*, Ch. 2).

name: The Euler–Poincaré theorem in abelian K₀
text: for a bounded cochain complex over an abelian category the alternating sum of the classes of its terms equals that of its cohomology, for every invariant additive on short exact sequences, so the K₀-valued Euler characteristic is a quasi-isomorphism invariant (Weibel, *The K-book*, II.6.6).

name: Clifford's theorem, character form
text: for N ⊲ G finite and W irreducible over a splitting field, Res_N χ_W = e · Σ_g χ_{gV} over a transversal of the inertia group of a constituent V, e the common multiplicity: the full identity, assembled from the single-orbit form of TauCeti#2667 and the multiplicity half of TauCeti#3766 (Isaacs, Thm 6.2).

name: Stability of optimal transport
text: under a liminf condition on the moving costs and a recovery-plan condition, optimal values converge to that of the limit problem and optimal plans accumulate only on its optimal plans (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 5.20).

name: The counting lemma for graphons
text: |t(F, U) − t(F, W)| ≤ e(F)·‖U − W‖□ for a finite simple graph F and graphons U, W on one probability space (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, 10.23); the coupling-primary cut distance δ□ is defined in TauCeti#4141, its triangle inequality still open.

name: The factorisation theorem for isogenies
text: for isogenies φ : W₁ → W₂ and ψ : W₁ → W₃ of Weierstrass curves over any field, ψ = λ ∘ φ for a unique isogeny λ exactly when ψ*F(W₃) ⊆ φ*F(W₂) inside F(W₁), with no separability hypothesis (Silverman III.4.11, there separable); so a degree-one isogeny is an isomorphism.

name: Linearly reductive groups are reductive
text: over an algebraically closed field a linearly reductive affine group has no nontrivial normal unipotent closed subgroup, so a smooth geometrically connected affine group of finite type with linearly reductive geometric fibre is reductive, in every characteristic (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.45).

name: Schanuel's lemma and the horseshoe lemma
text: for projectives relative to a Quillen exact structure: conflations K ↪ Q ↠ X and K' ↪ Q' ↠ X with projective middle terms have K ⊞ Q' ≅ K' ⊞ Q, and a conflation X ↪ Y ↠ Z with projective presentations of X and Z yields K ↪ Q_X ⊞ Q_Z ↠ Y with kernel an extension of the two syzygies (Bühler, *Exact categories*, §12).

name: The Burau representation
text: the unreduced Burau representation B_n → GL_n(R) over any commutative ring and unit t, σᵢ ↦ the block [[1 − t, t], [1, 0]] on strands i, i + 1, with determinant (−t)^(exponent sum), specialising at t = 1 to the permutation representation (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*); the reduced representation is not yet carved out.

name: The Fourier-coefficient recurrence for Tₚ
text: at every prime p and level Γ₁(N), aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(⟨p⟩f), on M_k(N, χ) with p ∤ N the classical aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + χ(p) p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(f), and at p ∣ N the Uₚ case (Diamond–Shurman 5.2.2); hence the Tₚ-eigenvalue of a normalised eigenform is aₚ(f).

name: The first inequality of genus theory
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree with |d| > 1, of either signature, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is at most t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2); TauCeti#3884 had the imaginary case, and the matching lower bound for real fields is still open.

name: Deligne's bigrading of a mixed Hodge structure
text: I^{p,q} = (F^p ∩ W_{p+q}) ∩ (conj F^q ∩ W_{p+q} + Σ_{j≥2} conj F^{q−j+1} ∩ W_{p+q−j}), with I^{p,q} ≤ F^p ∩ W_{p+q}, I^{p,q} ≤ conj F^q modulo W_{p+q−2}, functoriality, and equal to the Hodge decomposition on a pure structure (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.10); that ⊕ I^{p,q} is everything in general, and strictness, are the next steps.

name: The rational points of an elliptic curve are the class group of its coordinate ring
text: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over a field K, Mathlib's injective map W(K) → Cl(K[W]) sending an affine point to the class of its point ideal is surjective, so the group of rational points is the ideal class group of the affine coordinate ring, by a genus-one Riemann–Roch dimension count over K[W] (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3.4–5).

name: The Krull–Akizuki theorem
text: for a Noetherian domain A of Krull dimension at most one with fraction field K and any finite extension L/K, the integral closure of A in L is Noetherian, with no separability hypothesis on L/K and no claim that it is a finite A-module; Mathlib has the separable case via the trace pairing, and the general case runs on the length bound length_A(M/aM) ≤ dim_K V · length_A(A/aA) (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 11.7).

name: The spinor glue lattice D₈⁺ is the E₈ root lattice
text: an explicit isometry of integral lattices between E₈ and D₈⁺ = D₈ ∪ (s + D₈), built from Bourbaki's eight simple roots written in Conway–Sloane coordinates and closed by unimodularity of E₈ rather than by uniqueness of the even unimodular lattice of rank 8; the discriminant forms agree and H⊥/H is trivial for the spinor glue subgroup H (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 4).

name: The Frobenius–Schur trichotomy for compact groups
text: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, the indicator ∫ χ_π(g²) dg is 1, 0 or −1, being 1 exactly when Sym²V has a nonzero invariant, −1 exactly when Λ²V does, and 0 when neither; this extends the finite-group trichotomy of TauCeti#2206 to compact groups via Haar integration and Schur's lemma, while the reading of the three values as real, complex and quaternionic type is a separate step not yet taken (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II.6).

name: Kantorovich duality on finite spaces
text: for probability mass functions μ, ν on finite sets and an arbitrary real cost c, the minimum of ∑ c·A over transport plans A equals the maximum of ∑ φ dμ + ∑ ψ dν over potentials with φ_i + ψ_j ≤ c(i, j), both extrema are attained, and a plan and a feasible pair are simultaneously optimal exactly when the plan is concentrated on the contact set of the pair; strong duality comes from Mathlib's Sion minimax theorem, and the Polish-space duality is a later milestone (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1).

name: The general linear group is reductive
text: over every field and in every characteristic, GLₙ satisfies the geometric definition of reductivity: it is smooth and geometrically connected, and has no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup over the algebraic closure, since such a subgroup fixes a nonzero vector of the standard representation by Kolchin's theorem, normality makes the fixed space a subcomodule, and simplicity of the standard representation then makes it everything (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §12; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §2.4).

name: The product formula for algebraic function fields
text: for an algebraic function field F/k over an arbitrary constant field and z ∈ F transcendental over k, deg (z)₀ = deg (z)∞ = [F : k(z)], so every principal divisor has degree zero, degree descends to the divisor class group, ℓ(D) = 0 when deg D < 0, and (TauCeti#4410) a degree-zero divisor is principal exactly when ℓ(D) ≥ 1, exactly when ℓ(D) = 1 over an exact constant field (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.4.11 and Cor. 1.4.12).

name: The resolution theorem for K₀ of an exact category
text: in a Quillen exact category, for a class P of projectives containing 0 and closed under biproducts, the alternating class [Q₀] − [Q₁] + ⋯ of a finite P-resolution in K₀(P) depends only on the resolved object (Schanuel's lemma) and is additive on conflations (the horseshoe lemma), so the inclusion of P into the objects of finite P-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀ with inverse the Euler class; the K₀ statement only, not Quillen's higher-K version (Quillen, *Higher algebraic K-theory I*, §4; Weibel, *The K-book*, II.7.6).

name: The structure theorem for odd-dimensional Clifford algebras
text: over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form on a (2l+1)-dimensional space is M_{2^l}(F) × M_{2^l}(F) and its even subalgebra is M_{2^l}(F), completing the even-dimensional case of TauCeti#3655 by splitting along the central volume element and identifying the even part through a central idempotent of a simple ring (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, Ch. V; Fulton–Harris §20.1).

name: The Berg–Christensen–Ressel representation theorem
text: for V a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a function F on the involutive semigroup ℝ≥0 × V is positive definite, continuous and bounded exactly when it is the Laplace–Fourier transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0 × V; the existence half is new and closes the semigroup-Bochner milestone by a fibrewise Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder argument on the densities of the time slices, the uniqueness half having landed earlier (Berg–Christensen–Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups*, §4.2).

name: The Steinberg representation of GL₂(𝔽_q)
text: the augmentation subrepresentation of the permutation representation ℂ[GL₂/B] on the projective line: it has dimension q, its character at g is the number of B-cosets fixed by g less one, the boundary principal series Ind_B(1 ⊗ 1) of TauCeti#3549 has character 1 + χ_St, and ⟨χ_St, χ_St⟩ = 1 by the two Bruhat double cosets; irreducibility as a `Simple` object is not yet drawn from the norm-one identity (Fulton–Harris §5.2; Steinberg 1951).

name: The formal character of a finite-dimensional Lie module
text: the multiplicity function χ ↦ dim M_χ of a finite-dimensional module over a nilpotent Lie algebra with linear weights, as an element of the integral group algebra ℤ[𝔥*]; isomorphism invariant and additive on products, and for a Cartan subalgebra of a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero its coefficients are the honest weight multiplicities, supported on integral weights and Weyl-invariant; multiplicativity on tensor products is the next step (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §22.5).

name: The sheaf of rational functions on an integral scheme
text: 𝒦_X as an 𝒪_X-module sheaf, the pushforward of the structure sheaf of Spec K(X) along Spec K(X) → X, whose sections over every nonempty open are K(X) compatibly with restriction and into which 𝒪_X embeds as a subsheaf; the object Cartier divisors and 𝒪_X(D) are phrased in, with Mathlib supplying the function field but no sheaf carrying it (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6).

name: The Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions
text: every Bernstein function f on [0, ∞) has the form f(λ) = a + bλ + ∫₀^∞ (1 − e^(−λt)) dμ(t) with a, b ≥ 0 and μ a measure on (0, ∞) with ∫ min(1, t) dμ < ∞, and conversely every such function is Bernstein (TauCeti#320 defined the class); uniqueness of the triplet (a, b, μ) is the next step (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thm 3.2).

name: Riemann's theorem and the genus of a function field
text: for an algebraic function field F/k the defect deg D − ℓ(D) is bounded over all divisors D, its maximum defines the genus g = max_D (deg D + 1 − ℓ(D)), and ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g for every divisor, with equality once deg D is large when k is algebraically closed in F; the index of specialty i(D) = ℓ(D) − deg D − 1 + g is defined and vanishes in large degree, while Riemann–Roch itself waits on Weil differentials (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, I.4–I.5).

name: The Frobenius–Schur indicator of a compact group, read off invariant forms
text: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, ν₂(π) = 1 exactly when π carries a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form, −1 exactly when it carries a nondegenerate invariant alternating one, and 0 exactly when it carries no nonzero invariant bilinear form at all; TauCeti#4313 had the trichotomy through invariants of Sym²V and Λ²V, and the reading as real, complex and quaternionic type remains a further step (Bump, *Lie Groups*, ch. 2).

name: The Hodge decomposition as an equivalence
text: a family of subspaces H^p of a complex vector space with conjugation ω which is an internal direct sum, satisfies ω(H^p) = H^(n−p) and vanishes in low degree determines a pure Hodge structure of weight n with F^p = ⊕_(q ≥ p) H^q, and this is inverse to taking Hodge components, so pure Hodge structures of weight n are the same thing as their (p, q)-decompositions; TauCeti#3662 had the forward direction only (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1).

name: Central simple algebras over separably closed fields are matrix algebras
text: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a separably closed field K is K-isomorphic to M_n(K), by the Jacobson–Noether theorem applied to the division algebra in Artin–Wedderburn, so every separably closed extension of a field splits all of its central simple algebras; Mathlib has the algebraically closed case (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, §2.2).

name: Unramified abelian extensions over a quadratic field are multiquadratic
text: if M/ℚ is abelian, F ⊆ M is quadratic and M/F is unramified at every finite prime, then M = ℚ(√a₁, …, √aₙ) for squarefree integers aᵢ no nonempty product of which is a square, so [M : ℚ] = 2ⁿ; this is the field-theoretic half of the maximality of the genus field, whose arithmetic half — matching the aᵢ to prime discriminants — comes next (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: The half-disc residue theorem with enclosed poles
text: the generalized winding number of the boundary of the upper half-disc of radius R is 1 at every point inside it, ½ at the origin and 0 outside, so for f holomorphic off a finite set {0} ∪ S with at worst simple poles there and S in the open half-disc, the Cauchy principal value of ∮ f along that boundary is 2πi Σ_(s ∈ S) Res_s f + πi Res₀ f, the pole on the contour counting half; the version along the real diameter with the arc subtracted is the form real improper integrals consume (Henrici, *Applied and Computational Complex Analysis* I, Thm 4.8f).

name: Cartier divisors on an integral scheme
text: the sheaf 𝒦_X^×/𝒪_X^×, formed as a cokernel in sheaves of abelian groups rather than as a quotient of global sections, and its group of global sections Cartier(X) with the principal divisor map K(X)^× → Cartier(X); 𝒪_X(D) and the dictionary with line bundles are the next steps (Stacks 02AR; Hartshorne II.6).

name: The x − T map of an elliptic curve
text: for E: y² = f(x) over a field K of characteristic ≠ 2, with A = K[X]/(f) and T the class of X, the map E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² sending (x, y) to the square class of x − T (corrected at the 2-torsion, where x − T is a zero divisor) is a group homomorphism, because the classes of three collinear points multiply to 1; that its kernel is 2E(K), the descent computing E(K)/2E(K), is the next step (ported from Michael Stoll's *EllipticCurves*; cf. Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.1).

name: The Lie functor on morphisms
text: a smooth homomorphism φ of finite-dimensional real Lie groups induces a Lie algebra homomorphism Lie(φ) on left-invariant derivations, its differential at the identity, with Lie(id) = id, Lie(ψ ∘ φ) = Lie(ψ) ∘ Lie(φ) and φ(exp X) = exp(Lie(φ) X) (Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, ch. 3).

name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form is a direct sum of irreducible submodules, every Lie submodule having a complement (Humphreys, GTM 9, §6.3).

name: Irreducible highest weight modules are finite-dimensional exactly at dominant integral weights
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, an irreducible module over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra generated by a highest weight vector of weight λ is finite-dimensional if and only if λ is dominant integral (Humphreys, GTM 9, §21.2).

name: The Clebsch–Gordan rule for sl₂
text: in characteristic zero, V(m) ⊗ V(n) is the direct sum of explicit submodules isomorphic to V(m + n − 2k), 0 ≤ k ≤ min(m, n) (Fulton–Harris §11.2).

name: Strong Kantorovich duality on compact spaces
text: for a continuous nonnegative cost on compact pseudometric spaces and probability measures μ, ν, inf_π ∫ c dπ over couplings equals the supremum of ∫φ dμ + ∫ψ dν over continuous (equally, integrable) potentials with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), extending the finite-space duality of 25 August (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Thm 1.3); attainment of the supremum is not claimed.

name: Frobenius–Schur indicator 1 means realizable over ℝ
text: an irreducible complex representation of a finite group has ν₂ = 1 exactly when it is the complexification of a real representation; the new half builds the real structure from an invariant symmetric and an invariant Hermitian form, completing the trichotomy of 8 August (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §13.2).

name: Finite covering spaces form a Galois category
text: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, the covering spaces with finite fibres form a Galois category (SGA 1) with the fibre over a basepoint as fibre functor.

name: The valence formula at general level
text: for a nonzero weight-k modular form on a finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), Σ_P (2/|Stab_Γ P|)·ord_P f + Σ_c ord_c f = k·[SL₂(ℤ):Γ]/12, the cusp sum over the ⟨T⟩-orbits on SL₂(ℤ)/Γ with each order read in its own width; the level-one case was announced on 14 August (Shimura, Thm 2.20).

name: The Selmer group K(S, n) is finite, via its fundamental exact sequence
text: for a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and a set S of primes, 1 → 𝒪_S^×/(𝒪_S^×)ⁿ → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1 is exact, so K(S, n) is finite when Cl_S is finite and 𝒪_S^× is finitely generated, in particular for a number field and finite S — the three TODOs of Mathlib's `SelmerGroup.lean`; extended to finite étale algebras in TauCeti#4610 (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).

name: The Hecke ring of Γ₀(N) is commutative
text: the Atkin–Lehner anti-involution fixes every double coset Γ₀(N)xΓ₀(N), x ∈ Δ₀(N), so Shimura's criterion of 4 August makes R(Γ₀(N), Δ₀(N)) commutative, and the composite T_n = ∏_p T_{p^{v_p(n)}} satisfies T_{mn} = T_m T_n for coprime m, n (TauCeti#4720); the abstract Hecke ring is being upstreamed (mathlib4#41251, mathlib4#41277) (Shimura §3.3).

name: The kernel of the x − T map is 2E(K)
text: for E: y² = f(x) over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, the map μ : E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² announced yesterday has kernel exactly 2E(K), so E(K)/2E(K) embeds in the square classes of A = K[X]/(f) — the injectivity half of 2-descent (Silverman, AEC X.1).

name: The integral closure of a Dedekind domain is Dedekind, with no separability
text: for a Dedekind domain A and any finite extension L of its fraction field, the integral closure of A in L is Dedekind; Mathlib has this for separable L/K, and the Krull–Akizuki theorem of 25 August removes the separability, which now covers inseparable isogenies of elliptic curves (Bourbaki, *Commutative Algebra*, VII §2.5).

name: Deligne's bigrading is an internal direct sum
text: for a mixed Hodge structure the subspaces I^{p,q} of 24 August are independent and span the complexification, with (W_k)_ℂ = ⊕_{p+q ≤ k} I^{p,q}; recovery of F and the conjugation symmetry remain (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.8).

name: The principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q) is irreducible exactly off the diagonal
text: Ind_B^{GL₂}(α ⊗ β) is irreducible if and only if α ≠ β; and the Steinberg character takes the values q, 1, 0, −1 on central, split semisimple, non-semisimple and elliptic elements (TauCeti#4732) (Fulton–Harris §5.2).

name: The spin representation is irreducible in odd dimension
text: for a polarised quadratic space of dimension 2l + 1 over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the even Clifford algebra is all of End(⋀W), so the spin representation is irreducible — the type B companion of the half-spin dichotomy of 21 August (Fulton–Harris §20.2).

name: The excursions of a recurrent Markov chain are i.i.d.
text: for a Markov kernel on a countable state space and a state a₀ returned to infinitely often almost surely, the successive excursions from a₀ are i.i.d., and the chain is the image of the infinite product of the excursion law under concatenation (Norris, *Markov Chains*, Ch. 1).

name: Maximal integral curves and the escape lemma
text: a C¹ vector field on a boundaryless manifold has through each point a maximal integral curve on an open interval, and at a finite endpoint the curve has no cluster point, so it leaves every compact set; hence every C¹ field on a compact manifold is complete (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, 9.16, 9.19).

name: The representation ring
text: R(G), the split Grothendieck ring of FDRep k G under ⊕ and ⊗, with the character homomorphism R(G) → (G → k) whose image is exactly the virtual characters; injectivity is a later step (Serre, §9.1).

name: The invariant differential of an elliptic curve
text: ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) in the Kähler differentials Ω_{K(E)/F} of the function field, with ω ≠ 0 in every characteristic; that div ω = 0 is not yet proved (Silverman, AEC III.1).

name: The weak Mordell–Weil theorem
text: for an elliptic curve y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆ over the fraction field K of a Dedekind domain in characteristic ≠ 2, the subgroup 2E(K) has finite index in E(K), provided that for each irreducible factor p of the cubic the ring of integers of K[X]/(p) has finite class group and finitely generated unit group, as it does over a number field; proved by explicit 2-descent through the étale algebra K[X]/(f), adapting Michael Stoll's Lean development, and it is the finiteness that the descent argument for the Mordell–Weil theorem itself consumes (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).

name: The Fréchet–Kolmogorov compactness criterion in Lᵖ
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, on a proper normed abelian group with Haar measure and with values in a finite-dimensional real space, a family of Lᵖ functions that is bounded in Lᵖ, has translation increments ‖f(· + h) − f‖ₚ uniformly small as h → 0, and is uniformly tight is totally bounded, hence relatively compact; proved through Arzelà–Ascoli applied to ball averages, and it is the input Rellich–Kondrachov needs (Brezis, Thm 4.26).

name: Analytic sets are universally measurable
text: every analytic subset of a Polish space is measurable for the completion of every s-finite Borel measure (Lusin; Kechris, Classical Descriptive Set Theory, Thm 21.10), and hence the strict sublevel sets of a Borel c-transform in optimal transport are analytic, which makes c-transforms measurable in every finite-measure completion.

name: Strong approximation for algebraic function fields
text: for a function field F/k with exact constant field, a proper subset S of its places, finitely many P₁, …, Pᵣ ∈ S, targets fᵢ ∈ F and integers rᵢ, a single x ∈ F has ord(x − fᵢ) = rᵢ at every Pᵢ and is regular at every other place of S (Stichtenoth, Thm 1.6.5); proved from Riemann's theorem through the repartition space, in the form Goppa-code applications use.

name: The inflation–restriction exact sequence for continuous cohomology
text: for any topological group G, normal subgroup N and topological G-module M, the sequence 0 → H¹(G/N, Mᴺ) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M) of explicit continuous-cochain cohomology is exact (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.7)); Mathlib has the discrete-group version for Rep k G.

name: Shapiro's lemma for continuous cohomology in degrees 0 and 1
text: for a profinite group G, a closed subgroup U and a discrete U-module A, evaluation at 1 induces H⁰(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H⁰(U, A) and H¹(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H¹(U, A), the inverse built from a continuous section of G → G/U (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.4)); degree 2 is not yet covered, and Mathlib has the discrete-group statement.

name: Faithfulness of the Lie functor on connected Lie groups
text: two smooth homomorphisms out of a preconnected finite-dimensional real Lie group that induce the same map of Lie algebras are equal, by naturality of the exponential map and its local inverse near the identity (Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, Ch. 20).

name: The Weil differentials of a function field form a one-dimensional space over it
text: for F/k with exact constant field, the Weil differentials Ω (the k-linear forms on the repartition space vanishing on some A(D) + F, with F acting by (f·ω)(a) = ω(f a)) satisfy dim_k Ω(D) = i(D), the index of specialty, and dim_F Ω = 1 (Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.5.7 and Prop. 1.5.9); the canonical divisor, duality and Riemann–Roch itself are the remaining steps.

name: The Kähler differentials of a function field are one-dimensional
text: if x is a separating element of F/k (x transcendental over k and F separable over k(x)), then Ω[F/k] is a one-dimensional F-vector space with basis dx, and y ↦ dy/dx is a k-derivation of F with dy = (dy/dx)·dx (Stichtenoth §IV.1), obtained from formally étale base change of Kähler differentials along k(x) → F.

name: The affine simply-laced Cartan form is positive semidefinite with radical spanned by the marks
text: for Ãₙ, D̃ₙ, Ẽ₆, Ẽ₇, Ẽ₈ the symmetrized Cartan form is positive semidefinite and its radical is exactly the line ℝδ spanned by the marks (Kac, Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras, Ch. 4), and deleting the affine node leaves the finite Cartan matrix of type Aₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈ in Bourbaki's numbering.

name: The weights of the spin representation
text: in the Fock model ⋀W of a polarisation V = W ⊕ W' ⊕ L, the commuting Clifford bivectors ½(wᵢw'ᵢ − w'ᵢwᵢ) act diagonally with weights exactly the 2ˡ half-integer sign vectors ½(±1, …, ±1), each weight space a line (Fulton–Harris §20.1); the comparison with the abstract Bₗ and Dₗ root data is still to come.

name: The degree-zero class group of a function field is the class group of an affine model
text: restriction to a Dedekind model R ⊂ F is a surjection Cl(F) → ClassGroup R whose kernel is generated by the classes of the places at infinity, and when R has a single place at infinity and it is rational this restricts to Cl⁰(F) ≅ ClassGroup R (Hartshorne II 6.5); it is the general form of the elliptic-curve case announced earlier, E(K) ≅ ClassGroup of the coordinate ring.

name: The sheaf 𝒪(D) of a Weil divisor
text: on an integral Noetherian scheme regular in codimension one, the subsheaf of the sheaf of rational functions whose sections over U are the f with ord(f) ≥ −D(x) at every codimension-one point x ∈ U (Hartshorne II §6); D ≤ E gives 𝒪(D) → 𝒪(E), multiplication by g is an isomorphism 𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D − div g), so linearly equivalent divisors have isomorphic sheaves; invertibility for locally principal D is the next step.

name: Integrally closed subalgebras of a function field are holomorphy rings
text: the holomorphy ring ⋂ 𝒪ₚ over a set S of places is integrally closed in F, every k-subalgebra of F integrally closed in F is the holomorphy ring of the places at which its elements are regular, and S is recovered from its holomorphy ring (Stichtenoth, Thm 3.2.6 and Cor. 3.2.8).

name: The Mordell–Weil theorem
text: for an elliptic curve E over a number field K the group E(K) of K-rational points is finitely generated, and its torsion subgroup is finite; the descent runs from the weak theorem (TauCeti#4857) and the naive x-coordinate height with its approximate parallelogram law |h(P+Q) + h(P−Q) − 2h(P) − 2h(Q)| ≤ C and Northcott property (TauCeti#4882), with no canonical height involved (Silverman, AEC VIII.4).

name: The classification of real Clifford algebras
text: Cl(p, q) is isomorphic over ℝ to a matrix algebra over ℝ, ℂ or ℍ, or to a product of two matrix algebras over ℝ or over ℍ, according to (q − p) mod 8 and with the matrix sizes explicit, and the eightfold periodicity Cl(p+8, q) ≅ Cl(p, q) ⊗ M₁₆(ℝ) holds for every signature (Lawson–Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, Ch. I).

name: Kantorovich duality for lower semicontinuous costs
text: on compact metrizable spaces, for a lower semicontinuous cost c : X × Y → [0, ∞] the minimal transport cost inf_π ∫ c dπ over couplings of μ and ν equals the supremum of ∫ φ dμ + ∫ ψ dν over continuous φ, ψ with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), both sides allowed to be ∞; this extends the continuous-cost duality of TauCeti#4494 by monotone approximation (Villani, Topics in Optimal Transportation, Thm 1.3).

name: The Rellich–Kondrachov theorem on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)
text: for a bounded open Ω in a finite-dimensional real inner product space and 1 ≤ p < ∞, the inclusion W^{1,p}_0(Ω) → L^p(Ω) is a compact operator, with no regularity of ∂Ω assumed; the W^{1,p}(Ω) case under a Lipschitz boundary is a separate later milestone (Brezis, Cor. 9.16; Evans §5.7).

name: The Gagliardo–Nirenberg–Sobolev inequality on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)
text: for u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(Ω) and 1/p⋆ = 1/p − 1/n, ‖u‖_{L^{p⋆}(Ω)} ≤ C ‖∇u‖_{L^p} with Mathlib's explicit constant, giving the bounded embedding W^{1,p}_0(Ω) ↪ L^{p⋆}(Ω); Mathlib has the inequality for compactly supported C¹ functions, and the new content is the passage to their closure (Evans §5.6).

name: Flasque sheaves are acyclic
text: a flasque sheaf of abelian groups on a topological space has Hⁿ(U, F) = 0 for every n ≥ 1 and every open U; injective abelian sheaves and skyscraper sheaves are flasque, hence acyclic, by the classical dimension shift run through Mathlib's Ext-based sheaf cohomology (Hartshorne III.2; Godement).

name: The narrow genus field of a quadratic field
text: for squarefree d ∉ ℚ², the compositum of the fields ℚ(√P) over the prime discriminants P dividing the fundamental discriminant of d is abelian over ℚ, unramified over ℚ(√d) at every finite place, and contains every abelian extension of ℚ with those two properties, so any such extension has degree at most 2^t for t the number of ramified primes and is isomorphic to the compositum when the bound is attained; the infinite places are unconstrained, hence "narrow" (Cox, Primes of the Form x² + ny², §6.A; Lemmermeyer, Reciprocity Laws, §2.2).

name: The degree-zero divisor class group of a global function field is finite
text: for an algebraic function field F/k with k finite, Cl⁰(F) is finite, which defines the class number h_F = #Cl⁰(F); the proof counts places and effective divisors of bounded degree and uses Riemann's inequality, and Mathlib's `FunctionField.classNumber`, the class group of the ring of integers of one affine chart, is a different group whose comparison with Cl⁰(F) is a later step (Stichtenoth, Algebraic Function Fields and Codes, §5.1).

name: Kummer's theorem for the places of a function field
text: for a finite extension F'/F of function fields generated by y and a place P of F, the monic irreducible factors of the minimal polynomial of y reduced modulo P give distinct places over P whose relative degrees are at least the factors' degrees (TauCeti#4921), and when the prime of an affine model R is prime to the conductor of R[y] these are all the places over P, with residue degree the factor's degree and ramification index its multiplicity; the Dedekind-domain half generalises Mathlib's number-field Kummer–Dedekind computation of e and f to arbitrary Dedekind domains (Stichtenoth Thm 3.3.7, Cor 3.3.8).

name: The Kostka expansion of Schur polynomials
text: s_μ = Σ_ν K_{μν} m_ν in finitely many variables, writing a Schur polynomial in the monomial symmetric polynomials with the Kostka numbers of TauCeti#1684 as coefficients; that the two families are bases of the symmetric polynomials is not claimed (Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, I.6; Stanley, EC2 §7.10).

name: Tits systems and their Bruhat cells
text: a Tits system (BN-pair) is defined by subgroups B, N generating G with B ∩ N normal in N and simple reflections generating W = N/(B ∩ N) subject to BsB · BwB ⊆ BswB ∪ BwB and sBs⁻¹ ≠ B, and for every Tits system the double cosets BnB, n ∈ N, cover G, so N → B\G/B is surjective; GL₂(k) with its upper triangular subgroup and the normalizer of the diagonal torus is an instance (TauCeti#5005), and that distinct elements of W give distinct cells is not yet proved (Bourbaki, Lie IV §2; Humphreys, Linear Algebraic Groups, §28.1).

name: The unipotent radical
text: for an affine group scheme G of finite type over a field, R_u(G) is constructed as the greatest connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup, characterised by the universal property of its defining Hopf ideal and invariant under isomorphism (TauCeti#5039), and G is reductive exactly when it is smooth and geometrically connected with R_u(G ×_k k̄) trivial (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 6.42–6.46; Borel, Linear Algebraic Groups, §11.21).

name: The Fricke operator
text: f ↦ f ∣ₖ W with W = [[0, −1], [N, 0]], as a ℂ-linear endomorphism of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and of S_k(Γ₁(N)) (TauCeti#4455), which squares to the nonzero scalar (−1)^k N^{k−2} and so is an automorphism (TauCeti#4484), and which shifts the diamond operators by W ∘ ⟨d⟩ = ⟨d⁻¹⟩ ∘ W; this is the un-normalised operator, the normalised involution and the Atkin–Lehner operators W_Q being later rungs (Miyake, Modular Forms, §4.6).

name: Stieltjes functions
text: f is a Stieltjes function when f(t) = a/t + b + ∫₀^∞ (t + x)⁻¹ dμ(x) on (0, ∞) with a, b ≥ 0 and μ a measure on [0, ∞) with ∫ (1 + x)⁻¹ dμ < ∞; they form a convex cone (TauCeti#4957), and every Stieltjes function is completely monotone on (0, ∞), with dⁿ/dtⁿ ∫ (t + x)⁻¹ dμ = (−1)ⁿ n! ∫ (t + x)^{−n−1} dμ (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, Bernstein Functions, Thm 2.2).

name: The hook-length formula
text: for every Young diagram μ with n cells, the number f^μ of standard Young tableaux of shape μ satisfies f^μ · ∏_{c ∈ μ} h(c) = n!, proved by the Frame–Robinson–Thrall route through the beta-numbers βᵢ = λᵢ + r − 1 − i and the Frobenius determinant formula f^μ · ∏ᵢ βᵢ! = n! · ∏_{i<j} (βᵢ − βⱼ) (Macdonald I.1 Ex. 1, Sagan §3.10).

name: Schur–Weyl duality, the double centralizer
text: on (kⁿ)^{⊗d} over a field with d! ≠ 0, the image of k[S_d] permuting the tensor factors and the span of the diagonal operators f^{⊗d}, f ranging over all endomorphisms of kⁿ, are each other's commutants; that the invertible g^{⊗d} alone already span, and hence the statement for the image of k[GLₙ], is not yet proved (Fulton–Harris Lecture 6, Procesi Ch. 9).

name: Janiszewski's theorem
text: if two bounded closed sets S, T ⊆ ℂ have preconnected intersection and neither separates a from b, then S ∪ T does not separate them either; it is read off Borsuk's criterion, that a and b lie in one component of Kᶜ exactly when (z − a)/(z − b) has a continuous logarithm on the bounded closed set K, the input the Carathéodory boundary correspondence for Jordan domains is waiting on (Burckel §4, Munkres §§61–63).

name: The Fredholm alternative for the Dirichlet problem
text: for a bounded coercive divergence-form energy form B on H¹₀(Ω) with Ω bounded and any real κ, the weak problem B(u, v) − κ⟨u, v⟩_{L²} = ⟨f, v⟩_{L²} either has a nonzero homogeneous solution or has a unique solution for every f ∈ L²(Ω), the homogeneous solution space being finite-dimensional, via Rellich–Kondrachov and the abstract Fredholm alternative for compact operators (Evans §6.2.3, Gilbarg–Trudinger Thm 8.3).

name: Stone's theorem, the generator direction
text: the generator A of a strongly continuous unitary group on a complex Hilbert space is skew-adjoint, A† = −A, on its natural domain; strongly continuous one-parameter groups on Banach spaces are set up alongside (TauCeti#5154), with two-sided growth bounds, orbits differentiable on all of ℝ and uniqueness of the group given its generator, while the converse construction of e^{itH} from a self-adjoint H is not yet done (Reed–Simon Thm VIII.8).

name: The highest weight theorem for 𝔤𝔩ₙ
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every nonzero finite-dimensional 𝔤𝔩ₙ-module has a highest weight vector for the matrix-unit positive system and its weight is dominant integral (TauCeti#5150), two irreducibles with highest weight vectors of the same weight are isomorphic, and every weakly decreasing tuple of naturals is realised as a highest weight in an exterior power of the standard module (TauCeti#5169); the named irreducible for each dominant weight is still to come (Humphreys §20, Fulton–Harris §15).

name: The Gelfand–Tsetlin dimension formula
text: the number of Gelfand–Tsetlin patterns with top row λ equals the Weyl product ∏_{i<j} (λᵢ − λⱼ + j − i)/(j − i), proved from the branching recursion and a box-sum identity for integer Vandermonde determinants; this is an identity between a lattice-point count and a product, with no representation of GLₙ attached to either side yet (Fulton–Harris §15.3).

name: The type-A Chevalley–Demazure group is SL_{r+1}
text: the explicit full-weight Chevalley–Demazure carrier of type A_r built from the Kostant ℤ-form has points SL_{r+1}(K) over every field K, generated by its root subgroups, and the fixed points of its q-power Frobenius are SL_{r+1}(𝔽) for 𝔽 the fixed subfield, a finite group SL_{r+1}(q) in characteristic p (TauCeti#5193): the first finite group of Lie type the construction produces (Steinberg, *Lectures on Chevalley Groups*, §§3–4).

name: Local integral bases of function fields
text: for a finite separable extension F'/F of algebraic function fields and a place P of F, the integral closure of 𝒪_P in F' is free of rank [F' : F] over 𝒪_P with a basis that is an F-basis of F' (TauCeti#5118), and any fixed F-basis of F' is an integral basis at all but finitely many places (Stichtenoth Cor. 3.3.5, Thm 3.3.6).

name: The 27- and 56-dimensional minuscule representations of E₆ and E₇
text: the Chevalley generators of E₆ and E₇ realised as integer matrices on the minuscule weight orbits, with the Chevalley–Serre relations verified over ℤ and, for E₆, the coordinate lattice stable under the Kostant divided-power form (TauCeti#5204); no identification with the abstract irreducible highest-weight modules is claimed (Bourbaki Plates V–VI, Humphreys §13.4).

name: Frobenius's theorem
text: for a trivial-intersection subgroup H of a finite group G, the Frobenius kernel {1} ∪ (G ∖ ⋃ gHg⁻¹) is a normal subgroup and a complement to H, so G = N ⋊ H; closure of the kernel under multiplication is proved by Frobenius's character-theoretic argument, for which no character-free proof is known (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Ch. 7).

name: The irreducible representations of SU(2), classified
text: every finite-dimensional irreducible continuous representation of SU(2) is equivalent to the symmetric power Symᵈ(ℂ²) for exactly one d, with unitarity discharged by the unitarian trick rather than assumed; the analytic input is the Chebyshev identity χ_d = U_d(tr/2) and the uniform density of the character span in the continuous class functions (TauCeti#5282) (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II.4–5).

name: The Weyl denominator identity
text: ∏_{α>0}(1 − e^{−α}) = Σ_{w∈W} sgn(w) e^{w(ρ)−ρ} in the integral group algebra of the weight lattice of a finite crystallographic root system, proved combinatorially for an abstract root pairing with no Lie algebra entering; it is the denominator half of the Weyl character formula, whose Verma-character half is still to come (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §24).

name: The hook-content formula
text: for a partition μ with at most n rows the Weyl dimension ∏_{i<j}(λᵢ − λⱼ + j − i)/(j − i) equals ∏_{(i,j)∈μ}(n + j − i)/h(i,j), each cell contributing n plus its content over its hook length, stated division-free over ℕ; identifying this number with the dimension of an irreducible GLₙ representation is a separate later step (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, Thm 6.3).

name: The Schur polynomials are a basis
text: over any commutative ring, the polynomials in m variables that are symmetric and homogeneous of degree n form a free module with the Schur polynomials, indexed by the partitions of n into at most m parts, as a basis, the change of basis from the monomial symmetric polynomials being the unitriangular Kostka matrix (Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, I.6).

name: Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures
text: a morphism of mixed Hodge structures is strict for both filtrations, im f ∩ W′ₖ = f(Wₖ) and im f ∩ F′ᵖ = f(Fᵖ), proved by recovering the Hodge filtration from Deligne's bigrading; this is the theorem behind the abelian-ness of the category of mixed Hodge structures, a packaging still to come (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*; Peters–Steenbrink, *Mixed Hodge Structures*).

name: The Garnir relations
text: for a Garnir set X straddling two adjacent columns of a Young tableau t, the signed sum Σ_σ sgn(σ)σ over the permutations of X annihilates the polytabloid e_t; these are the relations that straighten arbitrary polytabloids, and the standard basis of the Specht module built on them is a later step (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, §7).

name: The chi-squared distribution
text: χ²ₖ for real k ≥ 0, with density, cdf P(k/2, x/2), mean k, variance 2k, mgf (1 − 2t)^(−k/2), characteristic function (1 − 2it)^(−k/2), and additivity of degrees of freedom under convolution; the characteristic function of the gamma distribution is proved along the way, by analytic continuation of the moment generating function.

name: The reduced Burau representation
text: the rank-n invariant-subspace form of the unreduced Burau representation of TauCeti#4218, now carved out explicitly with the two-strand normalization σ₀ ↦ −t; this is the representation the braid-closure algorithm for the Alexander polynomial runs on (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*, Ch. 3).

name: The Auslander–Reiten transpose
text: Tr M, the cokernel of the dual of a projective presentation P₁ → P₀ → M → 0, shown independent of the chosen minimal presentation and vanishing on projectives; the construction from which the Auslander–Reiten translate τ = D Tr and AR duality will be formed (Auslander–Reiten–Smalø, *Representation Theory of Artin Algebras*, IV.1).

name: The solvable radical
text: R(G) for a finite-type affine group scheme, the greatest connected normal smooth closed subgroup with geometrically solvable points, with its universal property, the containment of the unipotent radical, and the characterization of semisimplicity as triviality of R(G) after base change to an algebraic closure (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 6.42–6.46).

name: Hurwitz's theorem, both directions
text: the previously announced nonvanishing direction is joined by the localization of zeros: every zero of a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is a limit of zeros of the approximants, both halves read off one Rouché estimate (coordinated with the Riemann-mapping work in mathlib4#33505). (TauCeti#1646; the nonvanishing form came from TauCeti#1209)

name: The length–area inequality and Wolff's lemma
text: the Dirichlet integral of a holomorphic function controls the squared lengths of its circle images, so on every annulus some circle has a quantitatively short image: the classical length–area method, with Wolff's lemma as its short-circle consequence.

name: The Schwarz–Pick theorem, with rigidity
text: a holomorphic self-map of the disc contracts the pseudo-hyperbolic distance, and a single equality forces it to be a biholomorphism of the disc with explicit Möbius inverse; this upgrades the infinitesimal inequality announced earlier to the distance form with its equality case (coordinated with mathlib4#33505).

name: The monodromy theorem, global form
text: on a simply connected domain, a germ that continues analytically along every path is the germ of a single holomorphic function on the whole domain; the global corollary of the homotopy form announced earlier.

name: Geodesics in the Poincaré disc
text: the unit disc with the hyperbolic distance is a geodesic metric space, and the geodesic between two points is unique.

name: Jordan curves and Jordan domains
text: subsets homeomorphic to the circle, and the planar domains they bound: the definitions and basic API; the Jordan curve theorem itself is not claimed.

name: Grid links: grid diagrams modulo grid moves
text: the quotient of grid diagrams of all sizes by cyclic permutation, commutation, and stabilization: the combinatorial notion of link that grid homology (Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó) computes with, joining the grid-state gradings announced earlier; the comparison with embedded links is a separate later target.

name: Elementary and hyperelementary groups
text: the classes of finite groups against which Artin's and Brauer's induction theorems are stated, with the closure properties they are used through; the induction theorems themselves are later targets.

name: The Skolem–Noether theorem
text: two `K`-algebra homomorphisms from a finite-dimensional central simple algebra into a finite-dimensional simple algebra are conjugate by a unit; in particular every algebra automorphism of a finite-dimensional central simple algebra is inner.

name: The strong maximum principle for planar harmonic functions
text: a harmonic function on a preconnected open subset of the plane attaining an interior local maximum or minimum is constant there, by globalizing the zero case of the planar Harnack inequality announced earlier.

name: Schur orthogonality for compact groups
text: the first orthogonality relation for matrix coefficients of a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation of a compact group under Haar averaging, with the irreducible characters an orthonormal system in `L²` (the Haar-measure counterpart of Mathlib's finite-group `Representation.char_orthonormal`).

name: The isometries of the Poincaré disc, classified
text: every isometry of the hyperbolic distance on the unit disc is a disc automorphism or the conjugate of one, with the automorphism group parametrised by a rotation and a centre; the geodesics announced in the previous update now sit inside a classified isometry group.

name: A strongly continuous semigroup is determined by its generator
text: two C₀-semigroups on a Banach space with the same infinitesimal generator are equal.

name: The longest element of a finite Weyl group
text: the element `w₀` whose inversion set is the full set of positive roots, with the characterizations that an element with no inversions is the identity and that `w₀` maximizes the inversion count.

name: Kostka numbers
text: counting semistandard Young tableaux by shape and content, with the dominance triangularity (`K_{μμ} = 1`, and `K_{μν} = 0` unless `μ` dominates `ν`) and conjugation of partitions reversing the dominance order.

name: Brauer diagrams
text: perfect matchings of the `2k` boundary points of a diagram, counted by `(2k − 1)‼` — the combinatorics indexing the basis of the Brauer algebra, the centralizer of the orthogonal and symplectic actions on tensor powers.

name: E₄ and E₆ generate the level-one modular forms
text: every modular form for SL₂(ℤ) is a polynomial in the Eisenstein series E₄ and E₆ (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII.3); this ports Chris Birkbeck's open upstream draft mathlib4#39258 onto the current Mathlib pin.

name: Tangent vectors are point derivations
text: on a finite-dimensional Hausdorff real manifold, directional differentiation is a linear equivalence between the tangent space at an interior point and the algebraic point derivations on smooth functions, so the geometric and derivation definitions of the tangent space agree (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*).

name: Diagonalizable group schemes are classified by their characters
text: over a field, M ↦ Spec k[M] is an anti-equivalence from finitely generated commutative groups to the group schemes whose coordinate Hopf algebra is spanned by group-like elements (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.8–12.9). (TauCeti#1816, with the essential image characterized in TauCeti#1709)

name: Closed subgroup schemes correspond to Hopf ideals
text: for a commutative Hopf algebra H over any commutative ring, I ↦ Spec(H/I) is an order isomorphism from the Hopf ideals of H (with reversed inclusion) onto the closed subgroup schemes of Spec H (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 3.15; Waterhouse, §16).

name: Representations of an affine group scheme are comodules
text: natural actions of the point groups A ↦ Hom(H, A) on the scalar extensions A ⊗ V correspond exactly to H-comodule structures on V, with no finiteness, flatness, or projectivity hypotheses (Milne, *Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes*, VIII).

name: The closed dominant chamber is a strict fundamental domain
text: every Weyl orbit meets the closed dominant chamber in exactly one point, and the stabilizer of a dominant weight is generated by the simple reflections in the walls through it (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, Ch. 1).

name: The extreme exchangeable laws are the i.i.d. laws
text: the extreme points of the convex set of exchangeable probability laws on ℕ → α, for α standard Borel, are exactly the i.i.d. product laws: the extreme-point form of de Finetti–Hewitt–Savage (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries*, Ch. 1).

name: The exponential map of a Lie group
text: evaluation at time one of the invariant one-parameter subgroup generated by a tangent vector, with the scaling, identity, and inverse laws and smoothness of the generated subgroup, for groups modeled on a complete normed space.

name: Weyl modules for GL n
text: Weyl's construction: a Young symmetrizer acting on a tensor power of the standard representation cuts out a GL n-subrepresentation depending, up to isomorphism, only on the shape, and nonzero exactly when the shape has at most n rows (Fulton–Harris, Lecture 6).

name: The Sturm bound for finite-index subgroups
text: a modular form of weight k for a finite-index subgroup Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) whose q-expansion at ∞ vanishes to order beyond k·[SL₂(ℤ):Γ]/12 is zero, and the space of such forms is finite-dimensional; Mathlib master has the level-one case, and this ports the general case from Chris Birkbeck's open draft mathlib4#39000 (Sturm 1987; Diamond–Shurman).

name: The level-one modular forms are ℂ[E₄, E₆]
text: E₄ and E₆ are algebraically independent, upgrading the generation statement announced yesterday (TauCeti#1878) to an algebra isomorphism M(SL₂(ℤ)) ≅ ℂ[E₄, E₆] (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII).

name: Shimura's Hecke ring, commutative under an anti-involution
text: the free module on the double cosets H\Δ/H carries a convolution product making it an associative unital ring, and Shimura's criterion — an anti-involution of Δ preserving H and fixing every double coset — forces it to be commutative, the mechanism behind the commutativity of the classical Hecke algebra via the transpose and elementary divisors (Shimura, Ch. 3, Prop. 3.8). (TauCeti#1937; the convolution ring TauCeti#1933, the double-coset API TauCeti#1879)

name: Strong approximation for SL₂
text: the reduction map SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) is surjective for every d (Shimura §1.6), the input that realizes every unit of ℤ/N as a lower-right entry in Γ₀(N).

name: The pairing of two permutation characters counts double cosets
text: ⟨Ind_H^G 1, Ind_K^G 1⟩ = #(H\G/K), the trivial-character case of Mackey's intertwining-number formula, proved by Burnside's lemma with no algebraic closure needed (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*).

name: The symmetric- and exterior-square character formulas
text: χ_Sym²(g) = (χ(g)² + χ(g²))/2 and χ_Λ²(g) = (χ(g)² − χ(g²))/2, with division-free doubled forms valid over every field (Fulton–Harris, §2.1).

name: The central character of an irreducible representation
text: the scalar action ω_χ of the centre of k[G] given by Schur's lemma, with the class-sum identity ω_χ(K_C)·χ(1) = |C|·χ(g) and the integrality of its values — the standard input to χ(1) ∣ |G| and to the Dixon–Schneider algorithm (Isaacs, Ch. 3).

name: The Frobenius–Schur indicator counts invariants in the two squares
text: for a representation V of a finite group G over any field in which |G| is invertible, ν₂(V) = |G|⁻¹ Σ_g χ(g²) equals dim (Sym²V)ᴳ − dim (Λ²V)ᴳ, with the companion splitting dim (V ⊗ V)ᴳ = dim (Sym²V)ᴳ + dim (Λ²V)ᴳ; the real/complex/quaternionic trichotomy for irreducibles is a later milestone (Isaacs; Etingof).

name: The degree of an irreducible character divides the group order
text: Frobenius' divisibility theorem: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, χ(1) ∣ |G|, since the class-sum relation ωᵪ(K_C)·χ(1) = |C|·χ(g_C) and the algebraic integrality of character values make |G|/χ(1) a rational algebraic integer (Serre; Isaacs).

name: The Jacobson radical is left-right symmetric
text: the radical built from maximal left ideals agrees with the one built from maximal right ideals, through the elementwise criterion that every 1 + a·x·b is a unit; semiprimarity passes to the opposite ring and a left-Artinian ring is right Noetherian exactly when it is right Artinian, discharging the three standing `proof_wanted` declarations of Mathlib's `WedderburnArtin.lean` (Lam).

name: The centralizer theorem for central simple algebras
text: inside a finite-dimensional simple K-algebra A, the centralizer C of a central simple subalgebra B is again simple and dim B · dim C = dim A, through the identification C ≅ End of A over B ⊗ Aᵐᵒᵖ (Gille–Szamuely; Knapp).

name: The cusp-form L-series is entire
text: the Dirichlet series Σ aₙ n⁻ˢ of the announced modular-form L-function (TauCeti#1917) extends to an entire function for a cusp form of positive weight at arithmetic level: TauCeti#1987 rebuilt the interface on Mathlib's `ModularForm.L`, and the identity theorem transfers Mathlib's continuation (`CuspForm.differentiable_L`) across the half-plane identification — completing the milestone that bullet left open (Diamond–Shurman).

name: The Lie-group exponential is smooth
text: for a finite-dimensional smooth real Lie group, the exponential of TauCeti#1801 is C^∞ on the whole Lie algebra — Picard–Lindelöf parameter dependence gives smoothness near zero and exp(m·v) = (exp v)^m globalises it — with derivative at zero the identity (TauCeti#2005) (Hall; Duistermaat–Kolk).

name: The abstract and Banach-algebra exponentials coincide
text: on the unit group Rˣ of a finite-dimensional real normed algebra, the abstract Lie-group exponential recovers exp(x) = Σ xⁿ/n! under the canonical identification Lie(Rˣ) ≅ R, and specialises on GL(n, ℝ) to the matrix exponential with its diagonal, transpose, and conjugation formulas (TauCeti#1902) (Hall; Bourbaki LIE III).

name: Rouché's theorem for a null-homologous cycle
text: for f, g meromorphic on an open set U and a closed piecewise-C¹ cycle γ null-homologous in U with ‖f − g‖ < ‖f‖ + ‖g‖ on γ, the winding-weighted counts of zeros minus poles of f and g agree, extending the disc form of TauCeti#1179 off the circle in the symmetric two-sided phrasing (Conway).

name: Poincaré geodesics are Euclidean circles orthogonal to the unit circle
text: every geodesic line of the disc (classified in TauCeti#1512) traces a Euclidean diameter or 𝔻 ∩ ∂B(c, R) with ‖c‖² = R² + 1, the Pythagorean form of orthogonality to the boundary circle (Anderson).

name: The arithmetic Hecke triple for GL_n
text: the integral matrices of positive determinant lie in the commensurator of SL_n(ℤ) (Shimura's Lemma 3.10), founding the integral Hecke ring of GL_n on Mathlib's Hecke-triple class — the concrete arithmetic instance behind the announced Hecke-ring layer (Shimura §3.2).

name: Diamond operators and the nebentypus character spaces
text: the (ℤ/N)ˣ-action ⟨d⟩ on modular forms of level Γ₁(N), built through the Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) quotient on the strong-approximation input of TauCeti#1882, with membership in the χ-space the classical nebentypus relation f∣[k]γ = χ(d_γ)·f and the parity lemma — χ(−1) = (−1)^k on any nonzero space — in TauCeti#2013; ports the AINTLIB LeanModularForms development (Diamond–Shurman).

name: Gelfand–Tsetlin patterns
text: the triangular interlacing integer arrays indexing the Gelfand–Tsetlin basis of an irreducible rational GL_n-representation, with the top row a dominant weight as a theorem, the top-row-deletion bijection realising the branching recursion, and finiteness of the patterns over a fixed top row (Gelfand–Tsetlin; Molev).

name: The irreducible sl₂-modules, and complete reducibility
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a finite-dimensional irreducible module over a Lie algebra generated by an sl₂ triple has a unique highest weight n ∈ ℕ and is the standard module V(n) of dimension n + 1, and every submodule of a finite-dimensional module has a complement (TauCeti#2099), so every such module is ⨁ V(nᵢ); built on Mathlib's sl₂-triple and primitive-vector API, with V(n) constructed in TauCeti#2015 (Humphreys §7; Fulton–Harris).

name: The Krull–Schmidt theorem
text: two decompositions of a module of finite length into indecomposable summands are matched by a bijection of their index sets under which corresponding summands are isomorphic, in Azumaya's generality where one family need only have local endomorphism rings; the existence half and Fitting's lemma (TauCeti#1460) were already here, and this is the uniqueness they were missing (Lam; Anderson–Fuller).

name: The character table of a finite group
text: over an algebraically closed field in which |G| is invertible the irreducible characters are exactly as many as G has conjugacy classes and none is missing (TauCeti#2031), so they assemble into a square matrix carrying both orthogonality relations — orthonormal rows, and columns orthogonal weighted by class size — whose degree column consists of positive integers dividing |G| whose squares sum to |G| (Serre; Isaacs).

name: Continuous one-parameter subgroups are the exponentials
text: for a finite-dimensional smooth Lie group, X ↦ (t ↦ exp(tX)) is a bijection from the Lie algebra onto the continuous homomorphisms ℝ → G, so such a subgroup has a unique generator and is automatically smooth — the structural statement behind the exponential map of TauCeti#1801, shown smooth in TauCeti#1892 (Hall; Lee).

name: The Petersson inner product
text: the pairing ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫_D conj(f)·g·y^k dμ of modular forms over a fundamental domain, Hermitian and positive definite, with the integrand of a cusp form against a modular form integrable over the standard domain 𝒟; built on Mathlib's pointwise Petersson function and invariant measure, and ported from the AINTLIB LeanModularForms development (Miyake; Iwaniec).

name: The Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality
text: for an additive Haar measure on an n-dimensional real normed space, the centred maximal function Mf satisfies the weak-type (1,1) bound t·μ{x : Mf x > t} ≤ 4ⁿ ∫ ‖f‖, proved from Mathlib's Vitali covering lemmas; the first item of the harmonic-analysis lane the PDE roadmap builds on (Stein, *Singular Integrals* Ch. I).

name: James's submodule theorem
text: every submodule U of the Young permutation module M^μ satisfies S^μ ≤ U or U ≤ (S^μ)^⊥ for the tabloid form, and since that form is positive definite the two meet only at zero, so the Specht module — constructed from polytabloids in TauCeti#1984 — is irreducible over ℚ, giving the classical model of the irreducible representations of the symmetric group (James, LNM 682).

name: The nebentypus decomposition of M_k(Γ₁(N))
text: the diamond-operator character spaces announced in TauCeti#1959 are now shown to span M_k(Γ₁(N)) and to be independent, so M_k(Γ₁(N)) = ⨁_χ M_k(N, χ) as an internal direct sum, with the cusp-form analogue and a version relative to any diamond-invariant subspace (Diamond–Shurman §5.2).

name: Schur polynomials as tableau generating functions
text: the Schur polynomial of a partition in a finite alphabet, defined as the generating function of the semistandard Young tableaux of that shape weighted by content, with its coefficients identified as the Kostka numbers of TauCeti#1684 (Macdonald I.5; Stanley EC2 Ch. 7).

name: The Mackey irreducibility criterion
text: for H ≤ G finite and A a finite-dimensional representation of H over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, Ind_H^G A is irreducible exactly when A is irreducible and, for every double coset HsH other than H itself, the restrictions of A and of its conjugate ˢA to H ∩ sHs⁻¹ share no nonzero intertwiner (Serre §7.4).

name: Marcinkiewicz interpolation, and the strong (p,p) maximal inequality
text: the diagonal p₀ = 1, p₁ = ∞ case of Marcinkiewicz interpolation, applied to upgrade the weak-type (1,1) bound of TauCeti#2095 to ‖Mf‖_p ≤ C_p‖f‖_p for every 1 < p < ∞, the classical strong maximal theorem (Grafakos, *Classical Fourier Analysis* §1.3.1, §2.1.1).

name: The Frobenius–Schur trichotomy
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the indicator of an irreducible representation is 1 exactly when it carries a nonzero invariant symmetric form, −1 exactly when it carries a nonzero invariant alternating form, and 0 exactly when it carries no nonzero invariant bilinear form — the orthogonal/symplectic/complex classification, and the milestone the indicator bullet of TauCeti#2011 left open (Serre §13.2; Isaacs Ch. 4).

name: The Weyl group acts simply transitively on the Weyl chambers
text: each vector regular for a base lies in the open chamber of exactly one Weyl-group translate of the base, so the closed dominant chamber is a fundamental domain and the action on chambers is simply transitive (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras*, §10).

name: The valuation spectrum of a ring
text: `Spv A`, the equivalence classes of valuations on `A` with the topology generated by the rational inequalities, ported from Chris Birkbeck's open upstream draft mathlib4#38009 as the opening target of the adic-spaces roadmap; landing alongside it are the two inputs toward its spectrality, the patch criterion of Wedhorn Proposition 3.31 (spectralSpace_of_isClopen_generateFrom, TauCeti#2278) and the calculus of pro-constructible subsets with the spectrality of their subspaces (TauCeti#2289, TauCeti#2290) — the spectrality of `Spv A` itself is the next milestone, not yet concluded.

name: The valuation spectrum is a spectral space
text: `Spv A` is spectral, assembled from the patch presentation of the space and the patch criterion for spectral spaces; this is the milestone the `Spv` bullet of TauCeti#2262 named as outstanding, now closed (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Theorem 4.9, from Propositions 4.7 and 3.31).

name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem
text: a function continuous on [0,∞) and completely monotone on (0,∞) is the Laplace transform of a **unique** finite positive measure on ℝ≥0; both directions were announced with TauCeti#1482, and what is new is uniqueness of the representing measure, which turns the correspondence into a bijection (Widder, *The Laplace Transform* Ch. IV).

name: The branching rule for Schur polynomials
text: setting the last variable to 1 expands a Schur polynomial as the sum of the Schur polynomials of the shapes interlacing it, the restriction rule from GL_n to GL_{n−1} in symmetric-function form, complementing the tableau definition of TauCeti#2156 (Fulton, *Young Tableaux* §2.2; Macdonald I.5 Ex. 3).

name: The embedding theorem for affine group schemes
text: every affine group scheme of finite type over a field admits a faithful finite-dimensional representation, a closed immersion into GLₙ, built from finite coefficient-generating comodules (Waterhouse §3.4). (TauCeti#2582, with TauCeti#2386, TauCeti#2457)

name: The Specht modules, irreducible and pairwise distinct
text: over ℚ the Specht module of every partition of n is an irreducible representation of Sₙ, and two are isomorphic only when the partitions agree — one irreducible per partition, via James's dominance lemma (James §4). (TauCeti#2091, TauCeti#2446, with TauCeti#2245)

name: Complete reducibility and classification for sl₂
text: a finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra generated by an sl₂ triple, in characteristic zero over an algebraically closed field, is an internal direct sum of finitely many irreducibles, each a standard irreducible of sl₂ (Humphreys §7).

name: The Brauer group is a group
text: `BrauerGroup K` carries its commutative group structure, multiplication induced by ⊗ and inverse the opposite algebra, supplying the structure upstream Mathlib's `BrauerGroup/Defs.lean` records as its first TODO (Gille–Szamuely §2).

name: The automorphism group of an elliptic curve with j ∉ {0, 1728}
text: over any field, an elliptic curve with j-invariant away from 0 and 1728 has automorphism group {±1}, uniformly in the characteristic (Silverman III.10).

name: The quadratic twist of a Weierstrass curve
text: an explicit model over any commutative ring with the transformation laws b₂ ↦ Db₂, c₄ ↦ D²c₄, c₆ ↦ D³c₆, Δ ↦ D⁶Δ for D = t² − 4n, elliptic whenever D is a unit; with the twist by a quadratic extension and, behind it, Galois descent for changes of variables and affine points (TauCeti#2268).

name: The Mackey decomposition formula
text: the character of Res_K Ind_H^G A is the sum over double cosets KsH of the characters of the Mackey summands Ind over K ⊓ sHs⁻¹, with the intertwining-number formula for dim Hom of two induced representations as its pairing form (Serre §7.3–7.4).

name: H² classifies factor sets
text: the class of a normalized 2-cocycle in Mathlib's `groupCohomology.H2`, equal for two factor sets exactly when they differ by a coboundary; with projective representations and their factor sets identified with modules over the twisted group algebra (TauCeti#2016).

name: The Poincaré inequality on a slab
text: in Friedrichs form: a C¹ function supported in {a ≤ xᵢ ≤ b} satisfies ‖u‖_p ≤ (b−a)‖Du‖_p for 1 ≤ p < ∞, and no inequality of this shape holds on the whole space (Gilbarg–Trudinger §7.8).

name: SL_n(ℤ) is generated by transvections
text: every integer matrix of determinant one is a product of elementary transvections; with Smith normal form over ℤ by determinant-one operations — positive diagonal, divisibility chain, unique (TauCeti#2048).

name: A separable extension of Dedekind domains ramifies at only finitely many primes
text: the ramification locus of a module-finite torsion-free extension with separable fraction-field extension is finite, complementing Mathlib's openness of the unramified locus (Neukirch III.2).

name: The GL(2) Hecke operators T(n)
text: on the announced GL_n foundation, the classical computation layer: the divisor-pair basis with T(n), deg T(n) = σ₁(n), and the recurrence T(p^{r+2}) = T(p)·T(p^{r+1}) − p·⟨p⟩·T(p^r) making the local Hecke algebra polynomial in T(p) (Shimura Thm 3.24).

name: The gluing lemma for transport plans
text: two plans sharing an intermediate marginal admit a joint law on X × Y × Z with the given (X,Y)- and (Y,Z)-marginals, the composition step transport theory runs on (Villani, *Optimal Transport* Ch. 1).

name: Huber rings, Tate rings, and Huber pairs

reference.text: Voyager, TauCeti#2263, TauCeti#2267, TauCeti#2272, TauCeti#2348, TauCeti#2291, TauCeti#2298, TauCeti#2304, TauCeti#2476, TauCeti#2508, TauCeti#2538, TauCeti#2541

text: the foundations of Huber's theory for the adic-spaces roadmap: bounded and power-bounded elements, rings of integral elements and Huber pairs, restricted power series A⟨T₁,…,Tₖ⟩ with the strongly noetherian condition, A° integrally closed, completions stay Huber/Tate, and the separating examples — ℤ_p is Huber but not Tate, ℚ_p and K⸨X⸩ are Tate (Wedhorn §5–6).

name: The Peter–Weyl theorem
text: for a compact Hausdorff group, the normalized matrix coefficients of a skeleton of the unitary dual — constructed, not assumed — form a Hilbert basis of `L²(G)`, and the representative ring they span is uniformly dense in `C(G)` (Peter–Weyl, *Math. Ann.* 97, 1927).

name: The Cartan–Dieudonné theorem, generation form
text: over any field of characteristic ≠ 2, the orthogonal group of a finite-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic space is generated by its reflections in vectors of invertible norm, the input for Pin surjectivity; Mathlib carries the real inner-product case with the reflection-count bound (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, I §2).

name: Mayer–Vietoris for the cohomology of sheaves of modules on a scheme
text: the exact sequence relating `Hⁿ(U ⊔ V, M)` to `Hⁿ(U, M) ⊕ Hⁿ(V, M)` and `Hⁿ(U ⊓ V, M)` with its connecting map, together with its vanishing consequences (Stacks Project, *Cohomology of Sheaves*, Mayer–Vietoris).

name: The Lumer–Phillips generation theorem
text: an operator on a real Banach space generates a strongly continuous contraction semigroup exactly when it is densely defined and m-dissipative (Engel–Nagel, Theorem II.3.15; Pazy, Theorem 1.4.3).

name: The uniqueness clause of Wedderburn–Artin
text: `Matᵢ(D) ≃ Mat_κ(E)` exactly when `ι ≃ κ` and `D ≃ E`, so the degree and the division ring of a matrix presentation of a simple Artinian ring are invariants, completing the existence statement announced earlier (Lam, *A First Course in Noncommutative Rings*, Ch. 1).

name: The valence formula
text: for a meromorphic weight-`k` level-one form, `Σ_q ord_q + ½·ord_i + ⅓·ord_ρ + ord_∞ = k/12`, with zeros and poles allowed at the elliptic corners `i` and `ρ`; ports Chris Birkbeck's LeanModularForms valence-formula development onto the current pin (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).

name: The Specht modules classify the irreducible rational representations of Sₙ
text: `μ ↦ S^μ` is a bijection from the partitions of `n` onto the isomorphism classes of simple `ℚ[Sₙ]`-modules, upgrading the irreducibility and pairwise distinctness announced earlier to the full classification (James, *The Representation Theory of the Symmetric Groups*, Ch. 4).

name: Root systems of the same Dynkin type are isomorphic
text: two root systems carrying bases of the same Cartan type are isomorphic as root pairings, the rigidity half of the Cartan–Killing classification (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, VI §4).

name: Existence of highest weight vectors
text: in characteristic zero, every nonzero finite-dimensional module over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra has a highest weight vector whose weight is dominant integral, and irreducible modules are highest weight modules (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §20).

name: The class group and unit group of the S-integers
text: for a Dedekind domain, `Cl(𝒪_S)` is `Cl(R)` modulo the classes of the primes in `S`, hence finite whenever `Cl(R)` is, and for finite `S` the `S`-units are finitely generated whenever `Rˣ` is — the two finiteness inputs of weak Mordell–Weil (Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, I §11).

name: Every symplectic vector space carries a compatible almost complex structure
text: every symplectic form on a finite-dimensional real vector space is compatible with some almost complex structure, the nonemptiness half of the standard statement, with contractibility not addressed (McDuff–Salamon, *J-holomorphic Curves and Symplectic Topology*, §2.2).

name: The Lie algebra of SLₙ is the trace-zero matrices
text: the tangent Lie algebra of the algebraic group SLₙ is Mathlib's classical `sl n`, over every commutative coefficient algebra (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §10).

name: Henkel's open mapping theorem
text: a surjective equivariant additive map from a complete first-countable nonarchimedean group onto a Baire space is open when the scalars carry a zero sequence of units, the open-mapping input for Wedhorn's Proposition 6.16 (Henkel, arXiv:1407.5647).

name: Shimura's Theorem 3.20 for GL₁ and GL₂
text: the `p`-local Hecke ring of GLₙ is the polynomial ring `ℤ[X₁, …, Xₙ]` on the diagonal prime double cosets, proved in the two cases the classical theory uses; ports the AINTLIB development (Shimura, *Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions*, Theorem 3.20).

name: Wedhorn's weighted restricted power series `A⟨X⟩_T`
text: the restricted power series of a Huber ring with power-boundedness weights `T`, now complete with its topology, functoriality, density of polynomials, and the universal property for power-bounded weighted variables (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, 5.49–5.50).

name: Bochner's theorem
text: a function on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space is continuous with positive-definite subtraction kernel exactly when it is the Fourier transform of a unique finite positive measure (Bochner 1932; Rudin, *Fourier Analysis on Groups*, Theorem 1.4.3).

name: Clifford's theorem, single-orbit form
text: for `N ◁ G`, the irreducible `N`-constituents of the restriction of an irreducible representation of `G` form a single `G`-orbit, and `G` permutes the isotypic components transitively; the inertia-group induction clause is a later milestone (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Theorem 6.2).

name: The strong exchange condition
text: a length-decreasing reflection deletes one letter from any word for a Weyl-group element, with the deletion condition and the subword property as corollaries, toward the Coxeter presentation of the Weyl group (Humphreys, *Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups*, §5.8).

name: The forms of an elliptic curve split by a quadratic extension
text: for `j(E) ∉ {0, 1728}`, a curve isomorphic to `E` over `L` is isomorphic over `K` to `E` or to its quadratic twist by `L`, and the two are distinct — the order-two `H¹(Gal(L/K), Aut E)` made explicit, upgrading the twist construction announced earlier (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.5.4).

name: The Frobenius–Schur involution count
