text: `#{g : g² = x} = Σ_χ ν₂(χ)·χ(x)` over the irreducible characters, upgrading the previously announced indicator to the square-root counting formula it exists for (Isaacs, Ch. 4).

name: The primitive central idempotents of a group algebra
text: `e_χ = (deg χ/|G|)·Σ_g χ(g⁻¹)·g` for each irreducible character, pairwise orthogonal and summing to `1`: the dictionary between the character table and the Wedderburn decomposition (Webb, *A Course in Finite Group Representation Theory*, §3.6).

name: Spv (A, I) is a spectral space
text: the subspace of valuations with `cΓ_v(I) = Γ_v` is spectral for any ideal `I` sharing its radical with a finitely generated one, extending the previously announced spectrality of `Spv A` to the subspace Wedhorn's retraction `r_I` runs on (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Lemma 7.5).

name: Weak derivatives on an open set
text: the distributional derivative against compactly supported smooth test functions, with almost-everywhere uniqueness and agreement with the classical derivative: the opening of the Sobolev development (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.2).

name: The split octonions
text: the split Cayley algebra over an arbitrary commutative ring, built as Zorn vector matrices: an 8-dimensional alternative composition algebra whose norm N⟨a, b, v, w⟩ = ab − v⬝w is multiplicative, with the rank-two equation, the flexible law and the three Moufang identities (Springer–Veldkamp, *Octonions, Jordan Algebras and Exceptional Groups*).

name: Tannakian reconstruction
text: an affine group scheme over a field is recovered from its representations: the algebra-valued points of a commutative Hopf algebra correspond multiplicatively to the tensor automorphisms of the fibre functor on finite comodules (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §9.4).

name: The Jordan decomposition of an algebraic group element
text: over a perfect field a point of an affine algebraic group is the commuting product of a semisimple and a unipotent point of the same group, acting on every finite-dimensional representation by the linear Jordan factors; this is the group-scheme form of the endomorphism-level decomposition announced earlier, reconstructed through the Tannakian equivalence above (Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §2.4).

name: The Frobenius isogeny
text: over a finite field with q elements the q-power map on the coordinate ring of a Weierstrass curve is an isogeny π_q of the curve with itself, of degree q (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, II.2.11).

name: Maximal subfields of a central division algebra
text: a finite-dimensional central division algebra D over K contains a subfield of degree exactly deg D, the square root of dim_K D, and that subfield splits D (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*).

name: The universal enveloping algebra is a cocommutative Hopf algebra
text: over any commutative ring U(𝔤) carries the comultiplication making every Lie generator primitive, together with its counit and the antipode x ↦ −x, which reverses products and is involutive (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, Ch. I).

name: The Schur multiplier as the obstruction to linearising a projective representation
text: the class in H²(G, kˣ) of the factor set of a projective representation depends only on the projective action and vanishes exactly when the representation is an ordinary linear one rescaled by units, and every class arises this way (Karpilovsky, *Projective Representations of Finite Groups*).

name: The Hungerbühler–Wasem bounded-integrand formula
text: the generalized winding number of a closed piecewise-C¹ immersion γ about s is still (1/2π)∫(x ẏ − y ẋ)/(x² + y²) dt when γ passes through s, provided the crossings are interior and C^{1,1} on each side, with boundedness and integrability of the integrand derived rather than assumed; the off-curve case was announced earlier (Hungerbühler–Wasem, arXiv:1808.00997, Prop. 2.3).

name: The differential of Ad is ad
text: differentiating conjugation on a Lie group at the identity in the direction X carries a left-invariant field Y to ⁅X, Y⁆ (Knapp, *Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction*, Ch. I).

name: The weights of a highest weight module
text: for a module generated by a highest weight vector v of weight λ over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra, with no finite-dimensionality assumed, every weight χ satisfies λ − χ ∈ Q⁺, the cone of nonnegative integer combinations of the simple roots, and the λ-weight space is the line K·v, so λ and v are pinned down up to a scalar (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §20).

name: Representations of a diagonalizable group are diagonalizable
text: a comodule over the monoid algebra R[G] is the internal direct sum of its weight submodules, on each of which a point of D(G) = Spec R[G] acts through the character g (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.12; Waterhouse §3.2).

name: The weak Sobolev space W^{1,p}(Ω)
text: the first-order Sobolev space on an open subset of a Euclidean space, cut out of the Lᵖ value-gradient jets by the distributional integration-by-parts identity and proved complete for every 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, with membership shown to be exactly weak differentiability with the recorded gradient (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, §5.2).

name: The spinor representation in its Fock model
text: for a polarization V = W ⊕ W' ⊕ L of a quadratic space, the exterior algebra ⋀·W is made a module over the Clifford algebra of Q, with exterior multiplication as creation, contraction against the polarization pairing as annihilation and the grade involution on the remainder; stated over an arbitrary commutative ring (Chevalley, *The Algebraic Theory of Spinors*).

name: The adic spectrum Spa(A, A⁺)
text: the continuous valuations on A bounded by 1 on the subring A⁺, as a subset of the valuation spectrum, with its membership criterion and antitonicity in A⁺; the point set only, with spectrality and the structure presheaf to follow, and also being formalised in mathlib4#42315, which instead bundles a chosen representative (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Def. 7.23).

name: The canonical commutation relation on Schwartz space
text: the annihilation and creation operators a = (x + d/dx)/√2 and a† = (x − d/dx)/√2 are continuous linear operators on the real Schwartz space 𝒮(ℝ, ℝ) with aa† − a†a = id, they ladder the Hermite functions by a ψₙ = √n ψₙ₋₁ and a† ψₙ = √(n+1) ψₙ₊₁, and the number operator N = a†a and the harmonic oscillator H = N + ½ have the ψₙ as eigenvectors with eigenvalues n and n + ½; the extension to unbounded operators on L²(ℝ) is a later milestone (Hall, *Quantum Theory for Mathematicians*).

name: The conditional strong law of large numbers
text: for a conditionally i.i.d. process with directing measure ν and a bounded measurable observable f, the averages (1/n)Σ_{i<n} f(Xᵢ) converge almost surely to ∫ f dν, so for an exchangeable process on a standard Borel state space the empirical frequency of each fixed measurable set converges almost surely to the mass ν gives it; the weak convergence of the empirical measures themselves needs a topology on the state space and is a separate later milestone (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, §1.1).

name: The valence formula
text: for a nonzero weight-k level-one form, Σ_q ord_q f + ½·ord_i f + ⅓·ord_ρ f + ord_∞ f = k/12, the sum running over the non-elliptic SL₂(ℤ)-orbits and the only hypothesis being f ≠ 0; the form announced on 11 August was the intermediate one, quantified over a finite divisor set with two capture hypotheses and summed over three explicit boundary families, and this is the textbook orbit-sum statement those were bookkeeping for (Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, VII §3).

name: Every reflection of a root system is realised by an automorphism of the Lie algebra
text: Chevalley's τ = exp(ad e)∘exp(ad(−f))∘exp(ad e) attached to an sl₂ triple negates and swaps the triple, fixes the joint centraliser of e and f, acts on a Cartan subalgebra as the coreflection y ↦ y − α(y)α^∨, and carries the root space L_β onto L_{β − β(α^∨)α}, so every reflection of the root system of a split Killing Lie algebra comes from an automorphism of the algebra (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, Proposition 14.3).

name: The adic spectrum is a spectral space
text: Spa(A, A⁺) is spectral for every Huber ring A and subring A⁺, exhibited as a pro-constructible subspace of Spv(A, IA); the point set went out on 13 August with spectrality named as still to come, and this is that step, reached through Wedhorn's Theorem 7.10, which identifies Cont A inside Spv(A, IA), and Corollary 7.12, which makes Cont A itself spectral; the space is also being formalised in mathlib4#42315 (Wedhorn, *Adic Spaces*, Theorem 7.35).

name: Kostant's rank-one straightening formula
text: in any associative ℚ-algebra whose elements E, F, H satisfy the sl₂ relations, E⁽ᵐ⁾ F⁽ⁿ⁾ = Σ_{k ≤ min(m,n)} F⁽ⁿ⁻ᵏ⁾ · (H − m − n + 2k choose k) · E⁽ᵐ⁻ᵏ⁾, with generalized binomial coefficients and no denominators — the normal-ordering rule that makes the Kostant ℤ-form of a universal enveloping algebra closed under multiplication (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §26.2).

name: Polarization for multilinear maps
text: for a multilinear map f of a finite family of arguments, Σ_{S ⊆ ι} (−1)^|S| f(Σ_{i ∉ S} mᵢ, …, Σ_{i ∉ S} mᵢ) = Σ_σ f(m_{σ(1)}, …, m_{σ(n)}) with no invertibility assumed, so the diagonal values of f already determine every symmetrization; over a ring in which (#ι)! is invertible this identifies the symmetric tensors of ⨂ M with the span of the pure powers ⨂ᵢ x (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory: A First Course*, Appendix B.1).

name: The Weyl character formula for SU(2)
text: the character of Symᵈ(ℂ²) on the maximal torus is χ_d(θ) = sin((d+1)θ)/sin θ off the multiples of π, where it is (d+1)cosᵈθ, together with the unconditional telescoped form sin θ · χ_d = sin((d+1)θ) that holds everywhere; this is the rank-one case, the general Weyl character formula being a later milestone (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II §5).

name: The degree of an isogeny is finite, positive and multiplicative
text: the function-field extension an isogeny of Weierstrass curves measures is finite, the inseparable case included, so deg φ is a genuine positive integer, it is 1 exactly when the function-field pullback is onto, and deg(ψ ∘ φ) = deg ψ · deg φ (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, II.2).

name: The Dirichlet integral
text: ∫₀^R sin(ax)/x dx → π/2 for every a > 0, evaluated along a contour that passes through the pole using the Hungerbühler–Wasem on-contour residue theorem.

name: A normalised EDS is an elliptic net
text: `normEDS b c d` satisfies the four-index elliptic relation over any commutative ring with no hypothesis on the parameters, giving the elliptic half of the `IsEllipticDvdSequence` TODO recorded in Mathlib's own EDS file.

name: Sard's lemma on the flat stratum
text: the image of the set where every derivative of order 1 to k vanishes is null; this is the higher-regularity dimension range, alongside the equal-dimension and dimension-increasing cases announced earlier.

name: The character table of Sₙ
text: the ℤ-valued character of each Specht module and the resulting table indexed by partitions; the earlier announcement was the character table of a general finite group, this is the concrete symmetric-group one together with integrality of the characters.

name: The local normal form of a Fredholm map
text: Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction: in suitable local coordinates a Fredholm map is a linear surjection paired with an obstruction map valued in a finite-dimensional space.

name: Finite exchangeability as sampling without replacement
text: Diaconis–Freedman: a finitely exchangeable law is the law of a sample drawn at uniformly chosen distinct indices from a random finite population.

name: Orders of the point stabilisers of the modular group
text: 4 at i, 6 at ρ and 2 at every other point of ℍ, established at every point rather than only inside the standard fundamental domain.

name: The simply connected root datum of type E₈
text: the pinned root datum, whose 240 roots come from a completeness proof for the norm-two vectors of the E₈ lattice rather than a tabulated reflection action.

name: Exact structures
text: Quillen exact structures on an additive category, built on kernel–cokernel pairs, in Bühler's axiomatisation.

name: The Cartan–Killing classification of finite-type Cartan matrices
text: every nonempty connected finite-type Cartan matrix is, after a simultaneous relabelling of rows and columns, the standard Cartan matrix of exactly one valid Dynkin type Aₙ, Bₙ, Cₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄, G₂, and hence every irreducible reduced crystallographic finite root system has a unique Dynkin type; together with the rigidity statement announced earlier (TauCeti#2532) this closes the classification the "Dynkin types" bullet (TauCeti#1431) explicitly left open (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras*, VI §4; Humphreys §11).

name: The Lie–Trotter product formula
text: on a finite-dimensional real Lie group, (exp(tX/n)·exp(tY/n))ⁿ → exp(t(X+Y)) as n → ∞ for left-invariant derivations X, Y, proved from a general power-limit lemma for curves whose local logarithm has prescribed derivative; this is the addition-closure input for the Lie algebra of a closed subgroup, with Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem itself a later milestone.

name: Weyl-group invariance of weight multiplicities
text: for a finite-dimensional module M over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, dim M_{w·χ} = dim M_χ for every element w of the Weyl group, so the set of weights is Weyl-stable; proved directly from the rank-one sl₂ theory along root strings rather than through Weyl's complete reducibility theorem (Humphreys §21.2).

name: The conjugacy classes of GL₂ over a field
text: over any field F, two non-scalar elements of GL₂(F) are conjugate exactly when they share trace and determinant (rational canonical form in size two), so the classes are indexed by Fˣ ⊔ (F × Fˣ), and GL₂(𝔽_q) has exactly q² − 1 conjugacy classes, the number of its irreducible complex characters (Bonnafé, *Representations of SL₂(𝔽_q)*, ch. 1).

name: Diagonalizable groups are linearly reductive
text: every finite-dimensional comodule over the monoid-algebra coalgebra k[G] of a commutative monoid over a field is completely reducible, so every diagonalizable group D(G) — split tori included — is linearly reductive over every field, with no finite-generation or connectedness hypothesis (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Thm 12.12; Waterhouse §3.2).

name: A normalised EDS is a divisibility sequence
text: `normEDS b c d k · complEDS b c d k n = normEDS b c d (n·k)` over any commutative ring with no hypothesis on b, c, d, so W(k) ∣ W(nk) for every k, n; with the elliptic-net half announced earlier (TauCeti#3270) this discharges both conjuncts of the `IsEllipticDvdSequence` TODO recorded in Mathlib's own EDS file.

name: Cartier duality over a general base
text: finite dualization is an anti-equivalence of the category of finite locally free bicommutative Hopf algebras over any commutative ring, extending the field case announced earlier (TauCeti#3290); the field case is separately transported through Spec to an anti-equivalence of finite commutative affine group schemes over a field (TauCeti#3307).

name: Projective covers and superfluous submodules
text: a submodule N ≤ P is superfluous when N ⊔ K = ⊤ forces K = ⊤, and a projective cover of M is a surjection P → M from a projective module with superfluous kernel; uniqueness up to an isomorphism commuting with the covering maps is proved, superfluous submodules are identified with the submodules of the Jacobson radical when the submodule lattice is coatomic, and existence over semiperfect rings is left for later (Anderson–Fuller, *Rings and Categories of Modules*, §17).

name: The half-spin representations
text: for a polarization V = W ⊕ W' of a quadratic space with no line summand, the exterior parity splitting ⋀W = ⋀ᵉᵛᵉⁿW ⊕ ⋀ᵒᵈᵈW of the spinor module is a splitting of the spin representation into two subrepresentations S⁺, S⁻, because the spin group lies in the even Clifford algebra and Clifford elements of parity i shift exterior parity by i; stated over any commutative ring, with irreducibility and dimensions of the summands not proved (Fulton–Harris §20.1).

name: The Hille–Yosida generation theorem
text: a densely defined operator A on a real Banach space whose resolvent powers satisfy ‖R(λ, A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ − ω)ⁿ generates a strongly continuous semigroup whose generator is exactly A, with growth bound (ω, M) (Engel–Nagel, *One-Parameter Semigroups for Linear Evolution Equations*, Thm II.3.8); the uniqueness direction was announced earlier, and this closes the milestone.

name: The finite de Finetti approximation
text: for m ≤ n, the m-coordinate marginal of an n-exchangeable process differs from the mixture of m-fold products of the empirical distribution of its n-population by at most m(m − 1)/2n, on every measurable event and in both directions (Diaconis–Freedman, *Finite exchangeable sequences*, Ann. Probab. 8 (1980)); the infinite de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski theorem was announced earlier.

name: The symmetric powers of the standard representation of SU(2) are irreducible
text: Symᵈ(ℂ²) is irreducible for every d, and two are equivalent exactly when their degrees agree, so they are pairwise inequivalent; the maximal torus alone cannot see this, and the argument turns on a single rational rotation in SU(2) with no vanishing entry. Exhaustion — that every finite-dimensional irreducible of SU(2) is one of these — is the remaining half of the classification.

name: Proximity invariance of the winding number
text: the "dog on a leash" lemma: closed curves with dist(γ₁ t, γ₀ t) < dist(γ₀ t, w) at every parameter have the same winding number about w. For piecewise-C¹ curves this yields invariance along the straight-line homotopy from the geometric hypothesis w ∉ [γ₀ t, γ₁ t] alone, with no regularity asked of the homotopy, where the form already available needed one that was C² on the square (Ahlfors, *Complex Analysis*, Ch. 4).

name: The Chevalley commutator relation in type G₂
text: for integral divided-power exponentials, E_x(t) E_y(u) = E_y(u) E_z(tu) E_w(t²u) E_v(t³u) E_s(t³u²) E_x(t): the case where the roots iα + jβ with i, j > 0 are α + β, 2α + β, 3α + β and 3α + 2β. No factorial is inverted, so it holds in arbitrary characteristic (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, Thm 5.2.2). The chain β, α + β, 2α + β for types B, C and F₄ is TauCeti#3513; the remaining G₂ pair α, α + β and the transport to the Kostant root subgroups are not done here.

name: Ad of the exponential is the exponential of ad
text: the tangent-space form of Ad(exp X) = exp(ad X) on a finite-dimensional real Lie group: the tangent adjoint action along the one-parameter subgroup generated by X and the operator exponential of ad X solve the same linear ODE with the same initial value, so uniqueness identifies them. This integrates the infinitesimal statement announced earlier (TauCeti#2840), which gave only the derivative of Ad at the identity.

name: A pinned simply connected root datum for every Dynkin type
text: the nine irreducible crystallographic families are assembled into one construction indexed by a valid Dynkin type, with proofs that the datum realizes its indexing Cartan type and that its coroots span the cocharacter lattice (Bourbaki, *Lie Groups and Lie Algebras* IV–VI, Plates I–IX). The last missing family was E₇, whose 126 coroots are proved to exhaust the norm-two vectors rather than tabulated (TauCeti#3461); E₈ was announced earlier.

name: Admissible lattices decompose into weight components
text: a subgroup of a rational representation stable under a Kostant ℤ-form contains every joint weight component of each of its elements, hence is the direct sum of the lattices it cuts out of the weight spaces (Humphreys, Lemma 27.1). The projector has to be built inside the form, from the binomial coefficients of the integer translates of a Cartan vector and Newton's forward-difference formula: the Lagrange interpolation projector has rational coefficients and need not preserve an integral structure.

name: The candidate genus field is unramified over ℚ(√d) at the finite places
text: for squarefree d not a rational square, every prime of 𝒪_K with K = ℚ(√d) is unramified in the compositum of the quadratic fields attached to the prime discriminants dividing the fundamental discriminant of d, including p = 2 and the primes dividing d. For d < 0 the candidate is therefore an everywhere-unramified abelian extension of K, hence inside its Hilbert class field; maximality and Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)² remain.

name: The identity component of an affine group is normal
text: for a commutative Hopf algebra of finite type over an algebraically closed field, the Hopf ideal cutting out the connected component of the counit point is stable under conjugation (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, Prop. 2.37). The component group is then the fppf quotient by it, with H(k)/H⁰(k) identified with the connected components of Spec H and so finite (TauCeti#3496); representability of that quotient and its finite étaleness remain.

name: Pure Hodge structures
text: weight-n purity as Deligne's opposedness condition on a bounded decreasing filtration F, that F p and the conjugate of F(n + 1 − p) are complementary for every p, with the pieces H^(p,n−p), the proof that conjugation exchanges H^(p,n−p) and H^(n−p,p), and the rank-one Tate structures ℤ(m) of weight −2m carrying the single nonzero piece H^(−m,−m) (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1). The conjugation is constructed, not assumed, as a canonical lattice-induced involution on an abstract complexification (TauCeti#3462); the internal-direct-sum decomposition is a separate target.

name: The discriminant form of an even lattice
text: for an even nondegenerate integral lattice the half-norm q_L(x + L) = B(x, x)/2 mod ℤ descends to A_L = Lᵛ/L, evenness being exactly what makes it independent of the representative; its polar form is the discriminant pairing B(x, y) mod ℤ, it is nondegenerate, and it is functorial under isometries (Nikulin, §1.1). The ℚ/ℤ-valued pairing is TauCeti#3469, the order formula #A_L = |det Gram(L)| is TauCeti#3474, and the unimodularity equivalences TauCeti#3473.

name: The elementary Chevalley group
text: over a commutative ring A, the subgroup E(A) = ⟨xᵢ(t)⟩ of automorphisms of A ⊗ M generated by the divided-power exponentials of the distinguished root vectors on a Kostant-stable lattice M, functorial in A, with the endomorphism induced by the pⁿ-power Frobenius that a Steinberg map is built from, injective once the value ring is reduced (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §4.4). Identifying E(k) with all points of the Chevalley–Demazure group scheme is not claimed.

name: The Bruhat decomposition of GL₂
text: over any field, GL₂ = B ⊔ BwB for the Borel subgroup B of upper-triangular matrices and the Weyl element w = (0 1; 1 0): B has exactly two double cosets, B and w together generate GL₂, and over 𝔽_q the big cell BwB has q²(q−1)² elements (Humphreys, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §28.3); this is the double-coset input the Mackey criterion needs for the principal series below.

name: The dot action of the Weyl group is free on the closed dominant chamber
text: for a root pairing with a base, w · x = w(x + ρ) − ρ; unlike the linear action, which is free only on the open chamber, no nontrivial Weyl-group element fixes a dominant weight under the dot action, so distinct dominant weights lie in distinct dot orbits and each is reached by a unique group element (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §23.3) — the separation statement the Harish-Chandra theory of central characters runs on.

name: The principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q)
text: for characters α, β of 𝔽_qˣ, the representation Ind_B^{GL₂}(α ⊗ β) induced from the Borel subgroup, of dimension q + 1, with the character of B inflated from the split torus and distinct pairs (α, β) giving distinct characters; the irreducibility criterion α ≠ β and the Steinberg constituent at α = β are not yet proved (Fulton–Harris, *Representation Theory*, §5.2).

name: The Jordan–Hölder multiplicity of a simple module
text: for a module M of finite length over any ring, [M : S] counts the composition factors isomorphic to S; every composition series from ⊥ to ⊤ computes the same number (Lang, *Algebra*, I §3, Jordan–Hölder), it depends only on the isomorphism classes of M and S, and it is the invariant the Cartan matrix cᵢⱼ = [Pᵢ : Sⱼ] of a finite-dimensional algebra is defined by.

name: Kolchin's common fixed vector theorem
text: a monoid acting by unipotent endomorphisms (each ρ(g) − 1 nilpotent) on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space over any field fixes a nonzero vector (Borel, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, Prop. 4.8); hence a reduced affine group of finite type over an algebraically closed field has only unipotent points iff it is a closed subgroup of some upper-unitriangular Uₙ (Springer §2.4).

name: The structure theorem for even-dimensional Clifford algebras
text: over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form on a 2l-dimensional space is the matrix algebra M_{2^l}(F), by a dimension count against the Fock model ⋀W of a polarization V = W ⊕ W′; the odd-dimensional case is not yet treated (Fulton–Harris §20.1).

name: Serre's relations in a split semisimple Lie algebra
text: for a split semisimple Lie algebra in characteristic zero with a base of its root system, the simple-root sl₂-triples satisfy (ad eᵢ)^{1 − ⟨αⱼ, αᵢ∨⟩} eⱼ = 0, so L is a quotient of the Serre algebra `Matrix.ToLieAlgebra` of its Cartan matrix by a map sending Hᵢ to αᵢ∨; injectivity of that map is not yet proved (Humphreys §18.1).

name: The Chevalley involution from integral structure constants
text: for a normalised family of root vectors x_α with ⁅x_α, x_{−α}⁆ = α∨, a Lie automorphism ω with ω(x_α) = −x_{−α} and ω = −1 on the Cartan subalgebra exists iff every structure constant N(α, β) is a Chevalley integer ±(p + 1), via the invariant N(α, β)·N(−α, −β) = −(p + 1)², and is then unique; producing an integrally normalised family, the other half of the Chevalley basis theorem, remains (Humphreys §25.2).

name: The Casimir element is central
text: for a finite-dimensional Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form, Ω = Σᵢ xᵢ yᵢ ∈ U(L), with (yᵢ) the Killing-dual basis of (xᵢ), is independent of the basis and central in the enveloping algebra; its eigenvalue ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ, ρ⟩ on highest weight modules is a separate target (Humphreys §6.2; Bourbaki, *Lie*, I §3.7).

name: Schur polynomials are symmetric, by the Bender–Knuth involution
text: the Bender–Knuth involution on semistandard tableaux of a fixed shape exchanges the multiplicities of v and v + 1 and fixes the others; reindexing the tableau generating function of TauCeti#2156 along it swaps adjacent variables, which generate Sₙ, so s_μ lies in the symmetric subalgebra (Bender–Knuth 1972; Stanley, EC2 §7.10).

name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem on the open half-line
text: a function completely monotone on (0, ∞) is the Laplace transform of a unique positive measure on ℝ≥0, now possibly infinite: the finite-measure form of TauCeti#2174 assumed continuity up to 0, and dropping it admits 1/t = ∫₀^∞ e^{−tx} dx, represented by Lebesgue measure (Widder, *The Laplace Transform*, Ch. IV Thm 12a).

name: The Hodge decomposition
text: for a pure Hodge structure of weight n given by a bounded opposed filtration F (TauCeti#3520), the components H^{p,n−p} = F^p ∩ conj F^{n−p} are independent, span the complexification, and recover F^p = ⊕_{q ≥ p} H^{q,n−q} — the internal direct sum the earlier announcement left open (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1).

name: Nikulin's overlattice correspondence
text: for a nondegenerate integral lattice L with discriminant group A_L = L^∨/L, the integral overlattices L ≤ M ≤ L^∨ correspond order-isomorphically to the subgroups of A_L on which the discriminant bilinear form vanishes, and for L even the even overlattices to those on which q_L : A_L → ℚ/ℤ vanishes (Nikulin, *Integral symmetric bilinear forms*, Prop. 1.4.1).

name: The Hecke operator at p ∣ N on modular forms
text: for p ∣ N the slash sum Σ_{b<p} f ∣_k (1 b; 0 p) descends to ℂ-linear endomorphisms of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) — the classical T_p at p ∣ N, the modern U_p — preserving each nebentypus space M_k(N, χ), S_k(N, χ), with a_m(T_p f) = a_{pm}(f) on q-expansions; the case p ∤ N, where a second coset adds χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{m/p}(f), is not yet built (Diamond–Shurman §5.2–5.3).

name: Sheaves are detected on a basis
text: covers by members of a basis of the opens of X form a coverage on Opens X generating the usual Grothendieck topology, so a presheaf valued in any category is a sheaf iff it satisfies the sheaf condition for basis covers alone — the construction Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sites.Coverage` docstring lists as an open project — and sheafhood on Spa(A, A⁺) is decided by rational covers (Stacks Tag 009H).

name: Couplings of two measures
text: `IsCoupling π μ ν`: a measure on X × Y with marginals μ and ν, stated for arbitrary measures, plus the bundled space of couplings of two probability measures; invariance under swap, pushforward and measurable equivalences, existence for finite measures iff the total masses agree, and uniqueness of the coupling out of a Dirac mass — the primitive object of the optimal-transport roadmap (Villani, *Optimal Transport*, Ch. 1).

name: Places of an algebraic function field
text: `Place k F`: a normalised discrete valuation of F/k, surjective onto ℤ and trivial on the constants, with its valuation ring 𝒪_P proved a DVR, the order function ord_P with the strict triangle inequality, the residue field F_P and degree [F_P : k], and a place determined by its valuation ring (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, §1.1).

name: The Coxeter functor of a quiver
text: C⁺, the composite of the Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev reflection functors along a sink-admissible ordering of the vertices, an endofunctor of the representations of a finite quiver; an indecomposable representation with finite-dimensional vertex spaces is either annihilated at some stage or carried to an indecomposable with dim(C⁺M) = c·dim M for the Coxeter transformation c — the engine of the BGP proof of Gabriel's theorem, whose height-descent argument is still to come (Bernstein–Gelfand–Ponomarev 1973).

name: Graphons, homomorphism densities and the cut norm
text: `Graphon Ω μ`, a symmetric measurable kernel Ω × Ω → [0, 1] on a probability space; the homomorphism density t(F, W) = ∫ Π_{ij ∈ E(F)} W(x_i, x_j) dμ^{V(F)} of a finite simple graph, in [0, 1] with t(F, W_p) = p^{e(F)} for the constant graphon; and the cut norm ‖K‖_□ = sup_{S,T} |∫_{S×T} K| of a bounded symmetric kernel, a seminorm with ‖K‖_□ ≤ ∫|K| (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, §7.1, §8.2).

name: The Morse lemma
text: at a nondegenerate critical point x of a smooth f : E → ℝ on a Banach space there is a chart ψ, smooth in both directions, with f(y) = f(x) + ½·D²f(x)(ψy, ψy) on its whole source — the Morse–Palais lemma, proved by Palais's square-root argument (Palais, Bull. AMS 75, 1969).

name: The classification of connected covering spaces
text: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, monodromy is an equivalence of categories from connected covering spaces to fibrewise transitive actions of the fundamental groupoid; the new half is reconstruction, quotienting the universal cover by a stabiliser (Hatcher §1.3).

name: The Poincaré inequality on W^{1,p}_0(Ω)
text: W^{1,p}_0(Ω) now exists as the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in the weak-derivative Sobolev space, and ‖u‖_p ≤ (b − a)·‖∇u‖_p holds on all of it when Ω lies between two hyperplanes at distance b − a, with the corollary ‖u‖_p ≤ 2R·‖∇u‖_p on a bounded Ω (Evans §5.6); the estimate announced earlier held for a single test function on a slab.

name: The genus-theory bound on the 2-rank of an imaginary quadratic class group
text: an imaginary quadratic field with t ramified rational primes has 2-rank Cl(K) ≤ t − 1, via the counting step of the ambiguous class number formula: every 2-torsion class contains a conjugation-stable ideal (integral Hilbert 90, TauCeti#3796), and every such ideal is a product of ramified primes up to a rational ideal (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, Ch. 3).

name: Hecke operators at every congruence level
text: every double coset of the Hecke triple (Γ₁(N), Δ₀(N)) now acts as a ℂ-linear endomorphism of M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) through Shimura's right-coset decomposition (Shimura, Prop. 3.37), and the normalisation lemma identifies the coset of diag(1, p) at p ∣ N with the classical U_p announced earlier (Diamond–Shurman, Prop. 5.2.1).

name: Representations of a quiver are modules over its path algebra
text: for a finite quiver Q over a field k, the category of representations of Q is equivalent to the category of left kQ-modules, the new half being essential surjectivity via the kQ-action on ⨁_v M_v (Assem–Simson–Skowroński, Ch. III).

name: The Hungerbühler–Wasem residue theorem for cycles
text: the generalized residue theorem announced earlier for one closed curve now holds for a null-homologous integer cycle of piecewise-C¹ immersions passing through the poles: the Cauchy principal value along the cycle is 2πi·Σ_s n_s(C)·Res_s f with non-integer generalized winding numbers, the form the paper states.

name: The relative Frobenius isogeny
text: over any field of characteristic p, the relative Frobenius F : W → W⁽ᵖ⁾ of a Weierstrass curve into its Frobenius twist, purely inseparable of degree p (Silverman, AEC II.2.11); the Frobenius isogeny announced earlier was the absolute q-power self-isogeny over a finite field.

name: Clifford's theorem, common-multiplicity half
text: restricted to a normal subgroup, an irreducible representation has all its irreducible constituents occurring with hom spaces of one common dimension, the common multiplicity e over a splitting field (Isaacs, *Character Theory of Finite Groups*, Thm 6.2); this completes the single-orbit form announced earlier, with the packaged decomposition into e copies of the conjugates still to come.

name: Némethi's lattice homology of a negative-definite plumbing is nonzero
text: an augmentation produces a class spanning a free 𝔽₂[U]-tower in the characteristic-two lattice homology of every negative-definite plumbing graph, the structure whose graded bottom carries Némethi's d-invariant; a companion result confines all homology below the top cubical degree (TauCeti#3833), while gradings and ℤ[U] signs are still to come.

name: The Kantorovich transport cost
text: the primal optimal-transport functional, the infimum of ∫ c dπ over the couplings π of two measures, with the predicate cutting out optimal plans and its elementary calculus (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1); the number the roadmap's existence, duality and Wasserstein layers are stated against.

name: K₀ of a Quillen exact category
text: the Grothendieck group cut out by [Y] − [X] − [Z] over the conflations of an exact structure, with its universal property and functoriality, alongside the split K₀ of an additive category identified with the group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes (TauCeti#3795; Weibel, *The K-book*, Ch. II).

name: Polarizations of pure Hodge structures
text: the Hodge–Riemann conditions on an integral bilinear form ((−1)ⁿ-symmetry, F^p ⊥ F^{n+1−p}, positivity of i^{p−q}·Q(x, x̄) on H^{p,q}), with the Tate structure as a polarized witness, together with the Weil operator C acting by i^{p−q} with C² = (−1)ⁿ (TauCeti#3870) — the two inputs the semisimplicity of polarizable Hodge structures runs through (Voisin, *Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I*, §7.1).

name: The ω division polynomials
text: the Y-coordinate half of the multiplication-by-n formula on a Weierstrass curve, completing the classical (φ, ψ) pair through 2ωₙ = ψcₙ − a₁φₙψₙ − a₃ψₙ³ (Silverman, AEC Exercise 3.7), the route the roadmap pins for Nagell–Lutz.

name: The ramified primes of an imaginary quadratic field span exactly 2^(t−1) classes
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d < −1 squarefree, the classes of the t ramified primes in Cl(𝒪_K) satisfy no relation beyond the one known one, so they generate a subgroup of order exactly 2^(t−1), giving the genus-theory lower bound 2-rank Cl(𝒪_K) ≥ t − 1; with the upper bound announced earlier (TauCeti#3796, TauCeti#3884) the 2-rank is now exactly t − 1 (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §3).

name: Irreducible highest weight modules are classified by their weight
text: over a split semisimple Lie algebra, two irreducible modules carrying highest weight vectors of weights λ and μ are isomorphic exactly when λ = μ, with no finite-dimensionality assumed, and every highest weight module has a greatest proper submodule with irreducible quotient, so L(λ) is well defined (Humphreys, *BGG Category 𝒪*, §1).

name: The Alexander polynomial of a Seifert matrix
text: the Conway-normalised Δ_V = T^(−g) · det(T·V − Vᵀ) over Laurent polynomials, symmetric under t ↦ t⁻¹, invariant under congruence and under the two enlargements that generate S-equivalence, with Δ(1) = det(V − Vᵀ), Δ = 1 for the unknot, and the classical values t − 1 + t⁻¹ and −t + 3 − t⁻¹ for the trefoil and figure-eight; the input is a Seifert matrix; a knot-embedding front end is separate later work (Lickorish, *An Introduction to Knot Theory*, Ch. 6).

name: Landau's theorem for Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients
text: a Dirichlet series with nonnegative coefficients has a singularity at its finite abscissa of absolute convergence: no function differentiable on a disc around σ agrees with the series immediately to its right (Hardy–Riesz, *The General Theory of Dirichlet's Series*).

name: Tori are reductive
text: every torus over a field is reductive, in arbitrary characteristic: every smooth unipotent closed subgroup of the geometric fibre is trivial (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.41).

name: The even Clifford structure theorem on half-spinors
text: for a polarized quadratic space with no line summand, the even Clifford subalgebra is End(S⁺) × End(S⁻) for the two half-spin representations, so invariant subspaces obey a strict dichotomy and every intertwiner between S⁺ and S⁻ vanishes, refining the full structure theorem Cl(Q) ≅ M_{2^l}(F) announced earlier (Fulton–Harris, §20).

name: The unit sphere is simply connected above rank two
text: the unit sphere of a real normed space of rank greater than two, in particular Sⁿ for n ≥ 2, is simply connected, by piecewise-linear interpolation, point omission and radial projection with no smoothing or simplicial approximation; this makes the library's π₁(ℝPⁿ) ≃ ℤ/2 unconditional, and the same sphere theorem is concurrently being formalised in mathlib4#28246 by a different route.

name: Continuous sections of profinite quotients
text: the quotient map of a profinite group by a closed subgroup admits a continuous section normalised at the identity, via a Zorn-and-Cantor construction of a closed transversal (Ribes–Zalesskii, *Profinite Groups*, Prop. 2.2.2).

name: The K(G,1) recognition principles
text: the orbit space of a free, properly discontinuous action of G on a weakly contractible space is a K(G,1), a path-connected cover of a K(G,1) is a K(H,1) for the subgroup H it recovers, and a space is aspherical exactly when its universal cover is weakly contractible — the machinery producing new K(G,1)s from old (Hatcher, §1.B).

name: The weight-space decomposition of rational GL n representations
text: every rational representation of GL n ℂ is the internal direct sum of its weight spaces under the diagonal torus, every joint eigencharacter being a monomial t ↦ ∏ tᵢ^(lᵢ), by Laurent expansion of the action and Artin's independence of characters (Jantzen, *Representations of Algebraic Groups*, I.2).

name: Abelian and triangulated K₀
text: the Grothendieck group of an essentially small abelian category, universal for invariants additive on short exact sequences and satisfying [X] − [Y] = [ker f] − [coker f] for every morphism f, together with the triangulated K₀ of a pretriangulated category, with [Y] = [X] + [Z] over distinguished triangles and [X⟦n⟧] = (−1)ⁿ[X]; these complete the four Grothendieck groups begun with the split and exact cases (TauCeti#3795, TauCeti#3829).

name: The dynamic parabolic, unipotent and Levi subgroups of a cocharacter
text: for a cocharacter λ : 𝔾ₘ → G of an affine group scheme, the subgroup functors P(λ), U(λ) and Z(λ) defined by limits along λ, with the Levi decomposition P(λ)(A) = U(λ)(A) ⋊ Z(λ)(A) on points — the dynamic route to parabolics that needs no root data (Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive Groups*, §2.1).

name: Separately and jointly exchangeable arrays
text: the two symmetries of a doubly indexed random array, law invariant under independent row and column permutations or only simultaneous ones, separated by an explicit witness, with de Finetti for the rows: the rows of a separately exchangeable array are conditionally i.i.d. — the first step of the classical route to the Aldous–Hoover representation (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Ch. 7).

name: The homogeneous Markov chain of a transition kernel
text: the path law of the Markov chain with initial law ν and transition kernel κ, built on Mathlib's Ionescu–Tulcea trajectory measure, with the Markov property, the marginal recursion, and the mass of a finite path as initial weight times transition weights (Kallenberg, *Foundations of Modern Probability*, Ch. 8).

name: The inverse function theorem for manifolds
text: a `C^n` map between boundaryless Banach manifolds (`1 ≤ n`) whose `mfderiv` at a point is a continuous linear equivalence is a `C^n` local diffeomorphism at that point — the converse of Mathlib's `IsLocalDiffeomorphAt.mfderivToContinuousLinearEquiv`, completing the characterisation of local diffeomorphisms by invertibility of the differential (Lang, *Differential and Riemannian Manifolds*).

name: Gauss's 2-rank formula for imaginary quadratic fields
text: for K = ℚ(√d) with d < −1 squarefree, the 2-rank of Cl(𝒪_K) equals t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes: the upper bound of TauCeti#3884 and the lower bound of TauCeti#3912 joined into the closed genus-theory equality (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §3; Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2).

name: The classification of covering spaces
text: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, monodromy is an equivalence of categories `CoveringSpace X ≌ (FundamentalGroupoid X ⥤ Type)`, extending the connected classification of TauCeti#3898 to all covering spaces; the disconnected case is rebuilt through a balanced-product construction over the universal cover (Brown, *Topology and Groupoids*; Spanier, Ch. 2).

name: The adjoint elementary Chevalley group
text: the first concrete instance of the parametrised elementary-group machinery of TauCeti#3506: for a Chevalley system the divided-power exponentials x_α(t) act on the adjoint Chevalley lattice over every commutative ring A, generating Carter's E(A), with the Chevalley commutator relation ⁅x_α(s), x_β(t)⁆ = x_{α+β}(N s t) for an integer structure constant N = ±(p + 1) (Carter, *Simple Groups of Lie Type*, §4.4, Theorem 5.2.2).

name: The division-polynomial formula for n • P
text: on the universal Weierstrass curve, n • (X, Y) = (φₙ/ψₙ², ωₙ/ψₙ³) for every n ≠ 0, and distinct multiples are distinct points: the closed form for multiplication-by-n that the ω division polynomials of TauCeti#3862 were built for (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, Exercise 3.7), ported from J. Xu and D. K. Angdinata's Nagell–Lutz development in AINTLIB.

name: The quaternionic recurrence for real Clifford algebras
text: adjoining two generators of square −1 tensors with the quaternions and swaps the signature, `Cliff(p, q + 2) ≅ Cliff(q, p) ⊗ ℍ`: the companion of the library's M₂(ℝ) recurrences and a standard step towards the mod-8 classification of real Clifford algebras, which remains later work (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, Ch. I).

name: The classical Hecke operator Tₚ at every prime
text: the double coset Γ₁(N)·diag(1, p)·Γ₁(N) splits into its p + 1 right cosets at a good prime (Diamond–Shurman, Proposition 5.2.1), giving Tₚ f = Σ_{b<p} f∣ₖ(1 b; 0 p) + (⟨p⟩ f)∣ₖ(p 0; 0 1) on `M_k(Γ₁(N))` and `S_k(Γ₁(N))` with no case split on the prime — at p ∣ N the diamond term vanishes and the formula degenerates to the Uₚ of TauCeti#3817.

name: The Casimir eigenvalue on a highest weight module
text: on a module generated by a highest weight vector of weight λ, the Casimir element of TauCeti#3750 acts by the scalar ⟨λ + ρ, λ + ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ, ρ⟩, the eigenvalue flagged there as a separate target and the key input to Weyl's complete reducibility (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §§22–23).

name: The preprojective algebra of a quiver
text: Π_k(Q), the path algebra of the doubled quiver modulo the relation Σ_a (a a* − a* a), with the vertexwise relations ρ_v proved to span the same two-sided ideal, so a map out of Π_k(Q) is checked one vertex at a time (Gelfand–Ponomarev; Crawley-Boevey's lectures on quiver representations).

name: The PL structure groupoid
text: piecewise-linear maps of real topological vector spaces (locally, a finite cover by convex polyhedra on each of which the map is continuous affine) satisfy Mathlib's pregroupoid laws, so PL manifolds — boundary and corner models included — are now `HasGroupoid M (PLGroupoid I)`, with the forgetful inclusion PL ⇒ Top (Rourke–Sanderson, *Introduction to Piecewise-Linear Topology*).

name: The volume element of a Clifford algebra
text: the ordered product ι v₁ ⋯ ι vₙ of a pairwise orthogonal spanning list is central for odd n, anticommutes with every generator for even n, and squares to (−1)^(n choose 2) · Q(v₁) ⋯ Q(vₙ), over any commutative ring with no invertibility of 2 — the extra central element behind the odd-dimensional Clifford centre (Lawson–Michelsohn, *Spin Geometry*, Ch. I).

name: The Morse–Sard theorem in finite dimensions
text: a sufficiently differentiable map between finite-dimensional real normed spaces, with no relation between the two dimensions, has a Haar-null set of critical values, so its regular values are dense; this completes, by Milnor's Fubini induction, the theorem whose one-dimensional, equal-dimension and vanishing-derivative slices were announced earlier (Milnor, *Topology from the Differentiable Viewpoint*, §3).

name: Existence of an optimal transport plan
text: for a lower semicontinuous cost on Polish spaces the Kantorovich infimum is attained: the couplings of two probability measures form a weakly compact set by tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, and the direct method produces an optimal plan, with attainment separated from finiteness of the optimal value (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 4.1).

name: The Dirichlet problem has a unique weak solution
text: for a divergence-form operator `L u = -∂ⱼ(aⁱʲ ∂ᵢu) + bⁱ ∂ᵢu + c u` with coercive energy form and `f ∈ L²(Ω)`, exactly one `u ∈ H¹₀(Ω)` satisfies `a(u, v) = ∫ f v` for all `v`, with the energy estimate `‖u‖ ≤ ‖f‖/C`, by Lax–Milgram; instantiated for the Poisson equation `-Δu = f` on bounded-geometry domains (Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, Ch. 6).

name: Gårding's inequality
text: the energy form of a uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator with bounded drift satisfies `(λ/2)‖∇u‖² − (β²/2λ)‖u‖²_{L²} ≤ a(u, u)` on `H¹(Ω)`, the lower bound behind the coercivity the Dirichlet theorem consumes (Evans, Ch. 6).

name: The inertia subgroups generate the Galois group of a number field
text: for `K/ℚ` finite Galois the inertia subgroups of the primes of `𝓞 K` generate `Gal(K/ℚ)`, since their fixed field would otherwise be an everywhere-unramified extension of `ℚ`, which Minkowski's discriminant bound forbids; the recorded consequence is the genus-theory step that an abelian extension of a number field unramified at all finite places has Galois group of exponent dividing the base degree (Serre, *Topics in Galois Theory*, §4.4).

name: Locally flat embeddings of codimension one are locally bicollared
text: a locally flat embedded `(n−1)`-manifold in an `n`-manifold has two-sided product neighbourhoods locally, with the converse over domains charted on the model space; the local half of Brown's collaring theorem, whose global statement is a separate later target (M. Brown, *Ann. of Math.* 75 (1962)).

name: The places of the rational function field, classified
text: the places of `k(x)` are exactly the monic irreducible polynomials together with the place at infinity, with residue field `k[X]/(q)` and degree `deg q` at the finite place of `q` and degree one at infinity, so the degree-one places are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`; built on Mathlib's Ostrowski-type classification of the valuations of `k(X)` (Stichtenoth, Prop. 1.2.1 and Thm. 1.2.2).

name: The coding representation of an exchangeable sequence
text: jointly with its directing measure, an exchangeable sequence in a standard Borel space is the coordinatewise image of an i.i.d. uniform sequence under one fixed measurable map, the same map for every process, and conversely every such coded law is exchangeable — upgrading the conditional-law form of de Finetti announced earlier to a functional representation (Kallenberg, *Probabilistic Symmetries and Invariance Principles*, Prop. 1.4).

name: Mixed Hodge structures
text: a rational weight filtration together with a Hodge filtration on the complexification whose weight-graded pieces carry pure Hodge structures, with the comparison `ℂ ⊗ grᵂ_k ≅ (W_k)_ℂ/(W_{k−1})_ℂ` proved, pure structures embedded as one-weight mixed ones, and the Tate structure as the first example; Deligne's `I^{p,q}` bigrading and strictness are later targets (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*; Peters–Steenbrink).

name: The Artin–Tits group of a Coxeter matrix, and the braid group
text: the group presented by the braid-word relations of a Coxeter matrix, with its universal property and canonical surjection onto the Coxeter group, and its type-A instance the braid group on `n` strands, mapping onto `Sₙ` with the pure braid group as kernel and nonabelian from three strands on; braid groups are also being formalised upstream in mathlib4#32941 (Brieskorn–Saito; Birman).

name: The Verma module
text: `M(λ)`, the quotient of `U(L)` by the left ideal generated by the kernel of the Borel character, with its universal property: every highest weight module of weight `λ` is a quotient of `M(λ)`, and `M(λ)` has a unique irreducible quotient `L(λ)`; nonvanishing of `M(λ)` is pinned to the linear-independence half of PBW, still open, and is proved for `λ = 0` (Humphreys, §20).

name: The error function
text: `erf` and `erfc` with oddness, strict monotonicity, the limits at both infinities and the derivative, giving the Gaussian cumulative distribution function in closed form, `cdf = (1 + erf((x − m)/√(2v)))/2`; the declarations follow the shapes of the open mathlib4#34053 so they can be swapped out when it lands (DLMF, Ch. 7).

name: The Sard–Smale theorem
text: the critical values of a C^k Fredholm map from an open subset of a second-countable Banach space to a complete normed space are meagre, so its regular values are residual and dense; at the threshold k ≥ (dim ker)² + 1, not yet Smale's sharp k > index (Smale, Amer. J. Math. 87 (1965)).

name: The Nagell–Lutz theorem
text: for A, B ∈ ℤ, a nonzero rational torsion point on y² = x³ + Ax + B has integer coordinates with y = 0 or y² ∣ Δ (Silverman, AEC VIII.7.1); the long-model form over the fraction field of any UFD — integral except at order two, where 4x, 8y are integral, with ψ₂² ∣ 4Δ — is TauCeti#4348 and TauCeti#4358.

name: The Temperley–Lieb algebra and the Jones representation of the braid group
text: TL_n(R, δ) by generators e₁, …, e_{n−1} and its three relations, shown not to collapse, and σᵢ ↦ a·1 + a⁻¹eᵢ at δ = −(a² + a⁻²), satisfying the braid relations and giving a nontrivial B_n → TL_n(R, δ)ˣ (Jones, Bull. AMS 12 (1985)); the Markov trace, hence the Jones polynomial, is not yet built.

name: The Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder theorem in finite-difference form
text: a function on [0, ∞) right-continuous at 0 whose mixed forward differences with nonnegative steps satisfy (−1)ⁿ Δ_{h₁}⋯Δ_{hₙ} f ≥ 0 is the Laplace transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0, and conversely, so Hausdorff's difference condition is equivalent to the smooth complete monotonicity of TauCeti#2174 (Widder, *The Laplace Transform*, Ch. IV).

name: Every Brauer class contains a unique division algebra
text: each class in Br(K) is represented by a finite-dimensional central division K-algebra, unique up to K-algebra isomorphism (Gille–Szamuely §2.4), and the kernel of Br(K) → Br(L) is exactly the classes split by L (TauCeti#4210).

name: Polarizable rational Hodge structures are semisimple
text: every rational Hodge substructure of a polarizable pure Hodge structure has an orthogonal complement for the polarizing form which is again a rational Hodge substructure and complements it over ℚ and over ℂ (Peters–Steenbrink, *Mixed Hodge Structures*, Ch. 2).

name: The Euler–Poincaré theorem in abelian K₀
text: for a bounded cochain complex over an abelian category the alternating sum of the classes of its terms equals that of its cohomology, for every invariant additive on short exact sequences, so the K₀-valued Euler characteristic is a quasi-isomorphism invariant (Weibel, *The K-book*, II.6.6).

name: Clifford's theorem, character form
text: for N ⊲ G finite and W irreducible over a splitting field, Res_N χ_W = e · Σ_g χ_{gV} over a transversal of the inertia group of a constituent V, e the common multiplicity: the full identity, assembled from the single-orbit form of TauCeti#2667 and the multiplicity half of TauCeti#3766 (Isaacs, Thm 6.2).

name: Stability of optimal transport
text: under a liminf condition on the moving costs and a recovery-plan condition, optimal values converge to that of the limit problem and optimal plans accumulate only on its optimal plans (Villani, *Optimal Transport: Old and New*, Thm 5.20).

name: The counting lemma for graphons
text: |t(F, U) − t(F, W)| ≤ e(F)·‖U − W‖□ for a finite simple graph F and graphons U, W on one probability space (Lovász, *Large Networks and Graph Limits*, 10.23); the coupling-primary cut distance δ□ is defined in TauCeti#4141, its triangle inequality still open.

name: The factorisation theorem for isogenies
text: for isogenies φ : W₁ → W₂ and ψ : W₁ → W₃ of Weierstrass curves over any field, ψ = λ ∘ φ for a unique isogeny λ exactly when ψ*F(W₃) ⊆ φ*F(W₂) inside F(W₁), with no separability hypothesis (Silverman III.4.11, there separable); so a degree-one isogeny is an isomorphism.

name: Linearly reductive groups are reductive
text: over an algebraically closed field a linearly reductive affine group has no nontrivial normal unipotent closed subgroup, so a smooth geometrically connected affine group of finite type with linearly reductive geometric fibre is reductive, in every characteristic (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, 12.45).

name: Schanuel's lemma and the horseshoe lemma
text: for projectives relative to a Quillen exact structure: conflations K ↪ Q ↠ X and K' ↪ Q' ↠ X with projective middle terms have K ⊞ Q' ≅ K' ⊞ Q, and a conflation X ↪ Y ↠ Z with projective presentations of X and Z yields K ↪ Q_X ⊞ Q_Z ↠ Y with kernel an extension of the two syzygies (Bühler, *Exact categories*, §12).

name: The Burau representation
text: the unreduced Burau representation B_n → GL_n(R) over any commutative ring and unit t, σᵢ ↦ the block [[1 − t, t], [1, 0]] on strands i, i + 1, with determinant (−t)^(exponent sum), specialising at t = 1 to the permutation representation (Birman, *Braids, Links, and Mapping Class Groups*); the reduced representation is not yet carved out.

name: The Fourier-coefficient recurrence for Tₚ
text: at every prime p and level Γ₁(N), aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(⟨p⟩f), on M_k(N, χ) with p ∤ N the classical aₘ(Tₚ f) = a_{pm}(f) + χ(p) p^{k−1} a_{m/p}(f), and at p ∣ N the Uₚ case (Diamond–Shurman 5.2.2); hence the Tₚ-eigenvalue of a normalised eigenform is aₚ(f).

name: The first inequality of genus theory
text: for K = ℚ(√d), d squarefree with |d| > 1, of either signature, the 2-rank of the narrow class group Cl⁺(K) is at most t − 1, t the number of ramified rational primes (Lemmermeyer, *Reciprocity Laws*, §2.2); TauCeti#3884 had the imaginary case, and the matching lower bound for real fields is still open.

name: Deligne's bigrading of a mixed Hodge structure
text: I^{p,q} = (F^p ∩ W_{p+q}) ∩ (conj F^q ∩ W_{p+q} + Σ_{j≥2} conj F^{q−j+1} ∩ W_{p+q−j}), with I^{p,q} ≤ F^p ∩ W_{p+q}, I^{p,q} ≤ conj F^q modulo W_{p+q−2}, functoriality, and equal to the Hodge decomposition on a pure structure (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.10); that ⊕ I^{p,q} is everything in general, and strictness, are the next steps.

name: The rational points of an elliptic curve are the class group of its coordinate ring
text: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve W over a field K, Mathlib's injective map W(K) → Cl(K[W]) sending an affine point to the class of its point ideal is surjective, so the group of rational points is the ideal class group of the affine coordinate ring, by a genus-one Riemann–Roch dimension count over K[W] (Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, III.3.4–5).

name: The Krull–Akizuki theorem
text: for a Noetherian domain A of Krull dimension at most one with fraction field K and any finite extension L/K, the integral closure of A in L is Noetherian, with no separability hypothesis on L/K and no claim that it is a finite A-module; Mathlib has the separable case via the trace pairing, and the general case runs on the length bound length_A(M/aM) ≤ dim_K V · length_A(A/aA) (Matsumura, *Commutative Ring Theory*, Thm 11.7).

name: The spinor glue lattice D₈⁺ is the E₈ root lattice
text: an explicit isometry of integral lattices between E₈ and D₈⁺ = D₈ ∪ (s + D₈), built from Bourbaki's eight simple roots written in Conway–Sloane coordinates and closed by unimodularity of E₈ rather than by uniqueness of the even unimodular lattice of rank 8; the discriminant forms agree and H⊥/H is trivial for the spinor glue subgroup H (Conway–Sloane, *Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups*, Ch. 4).

name: The Frobenius–Schur trichotomy for compact groups
text: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, the indicator ∫ χ_π(g²) dg is 1, 0 or −1, being 1 exactly when Sym²V has a nonzero invariant, −1 exactly when Λ²V does, and 0 when neither; this extends the finite-group trichotomy of TauCeti#2206 to compact groups via Haar integration and Schur's lemma, while the reading of the three values as real, complex and quaternionic type is a separate step not yet taken (Bröcker–tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*, II.6).

name: Kantorovich duality on finite spaces
text: for probability mass functions μ, ν on finite sets and an arbitrary real cost c, the minimum of ∑ c·A over transport plans A equals the maximum of ∑ φ dμ + ∑ ψ dν over potentials with φ_i + ψ_j ≤ c(i, j), both extrema are attained, and a plan and a feasible pair are simultaneously optimal exactly when the plan is concentrated on the contact set of the pair; strong duality comes from Mathlib's Sion minimax theorem, and the Polish-space duality is a later milestone (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Ch. 1).

name: The general linear group is reductive
text: over every field and in every characteristic, GLₙ satisfies the geometric definition of reductivity: it is smooth and geometrically connected, and has no nontrivial connected normal smooth unipotent closed subgroup over the algebraic closure, since such a subgroup fixes a nonzero vector of the standard representation by Kolchin's theorem, normality makes the fixed space a subcomodule, and simplicity of the standard representation then makes it everything (Milne, *Algebraic Groups*, §12; Springer, *Linear Algebraic Groups*, §2.4).

name: The product formula for algebraic function fields
text: for an algebraic function field F/k over an arbitrary constant field and z ∈ F transcendental over k, deg (z)₀ = deg (z)∞ = [F : k(z)], so every principal divisor has degree zero, degree descends to the divisor class group, ℓ(D) = 0 when deg D < 0, and (TauCeti#4410) a degree-zero divisor is principal exactly when ℓ(D) ≥ 1, exactly when ℓ(D) = 1 over an exact constant field (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, Thm 1.4.11 and Cor. 1.4.12).

name: The resolution theorem for K₀ of an exact category
text: in a Quillen exact category, for a class P of projectives containing 0 and closed under biproducts, the alternating class [Q₀] − [Q₁] + ⋯ of a finite P-resolution in K₀(P) depends only on the resolved object (Schanuel's lemma) and is additive on conflations (the horseshoe lemma), so the inclusion of P into the objects of finite P-dimension induces an isomorphism on exact K₀ with inverse the Euler class; the K₀ statement only, not Quillen's higher-K version (Quillen, *Higher algebraic K-theory I*, §4; Weibel, *The K-book*, II.7.6).

name: The structure theorem for odd-dimensional Clifford algebras
text: over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the Clifford algebra of a nondegenerate quadratic form on a (2l+1)-dimensional space is M_{2^l}(F) × M_{2^l}(F) and its even subalgebra is M_{2^l}(F), completing the even-dimensional case of TauCeti#3655 by splitting along the central volume element and identifying the even part through a central idempotent of a simple ring (Lam, *Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields*, Ch. V; Fulton–Harris §20.1).

name: The Berg–Christensen–Ressel representation theorem
text: for V a finite-dimensional real inner product space, a function F on the involutive semigroup ℝ≥0 × V is positive definite, continuous and bounded exactly when it is the Laplace–Fourier transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0 × V; the existence half is new and closes the semigroup-Bochner milestone by a fibrewise Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder argument on the densities of the time slices, the uniqueness half having landed earlier (Berg–Christensen–Ressel, *Harmonic Analysis on Semigroups*, §4.2).

name: The Steinberg representation of GL₂(𝔽_q)
text: the augmentation subrepresentation of the permutation representation ℂ[GL₂/B] on the projective line: it has dimension q, its character at g is the number of B-cosets fixed by g less one, the boundary principal series Ind_B(1 ⊗ 1) of TauCeti#3549 has character 1 + χ_St, and ⟨χ_St, χ_St⟩ = 1 by the two Bruhat double cosets; irreducibility as a `Simple` object is not yet drawn from the norm-one identity (Fulton–Harris §5.2; Steinberg 1951).

name: The formal character of a finite-dimensional Lie module
text: the multiplicity function χ ↦ dim M_χ of a finite-dimensional module over a nilpotent Lie algebra with linear weights, as an element of the integral group algebra ℤ[𝔥*]; isomorphism invariant and additive on products, and for a Cartan subalgebra of a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero its coefficients are the honest weight multiplicities, supported on integral weights and Weyl-invariant; multiplicativity on tensor products is the next step (Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*, §22.5).

name: The sheaf of rational functions on an integral scheme
text: 𝒦_X as an 𝒪_X-module sheaf, the pushforward of the structure sheaf of Spec K(X) along Spec K(X) → X, whose sections over every nonempty open are K(X) compatibly with restriction and into which 𝒪_X embeds as a subsheaf; the object Cartier divisors and 𝒪_X(D) are phrased in, with Mathlib supplying the function field but no sheaf carrying it (Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry*, II.6).

name: The Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions
text: every Bernstein function f on [0, ∞) has the form f(λ) = a + bλ + ∫₀^∞ (1 − e^(−λt)) dμ(t) with a, b ≥ 0 and μ a measure on (0, ∞) with ∫ min(1, t) dμ < ∞, and conversely every such function is Bernstein (TauCeti#320 defined the class); uniqueness of the triplet (a, b, μ) is the next step (Schilling–Song–Vondraček, *Bernstein Functions*, Thm 3.2).

name: Riemann's theorem and the genus of a function field
text: for an algebraic function field F/k the defect deg D − ℓ(D) is bounded over all divisors D, its maximum defines the genus g = max_D (deg D + 1 − ℓ(D)), and ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g for every divisor, with equality once deg D is large when k is algebraically closed in F; the index of specialty i(D) = ℓ(D) − deg D − 1 + g is defined and vanishes in large degree, while Riemann–Roch itself waits on Weil differentials (Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, I.4–I.5).

name: The Frobenius–Schur indicator of a compact group, read off invariant forms
text: for an irreducible unitary representation π of a compact group on a finite-dimensional complex inner product space, ν₂(π) = 1 exactly when π carries a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form, −1 exactly when it carries a nondegenerate invariant alternating one, and 0 exactly when it carries no nonzero invariant bilinear form at all; TauCeti#4313 had the trichotomy through invariants of Sym²V and Λ²V, and the reading as real, complex and quaternionic type remains a further step (Bump, *Lie Groups*, ch. 2).

name: The Hodge decomposition as an equivalence
text: a family of subspaces H^p of a complex vector space with conjugation ω which is an internal direct sum, satisfies ω(H^p) = H^(n−p) and vanishes in low degree determines a pure Hodge structure of weight n with F^p = ⊕_(q ≥ p) H^q, and this is inverse to taking Hodge components, so pure Hodge structures of weight n are the same thing as their (p, q)-decompositions; TauCeti#3662 had the forward direction only (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, §1.2.1).

name: Central simple algebras over separably closed fields are matrix algebras
text: a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over a separably closed field K is K-isomorphic to M_n(K), by the Jacobson–Noether theorem applied to the division algebra in Artin–Wedderburn, so every separably closed extension of a field splits all of its central simple algebras; Mathlib has the algebraically closed case (Gille–Szamuely, *Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology*, §2.2).

name: Unramified abelian extensions over a quadratic field are multiquadratic
text: if M/ℚ is abelian, F ⊆ M is quadratic and M/F is unramified at every finite prime, then M = ℚ(√a₁, …, √aₙ) for squarefree integers aᵢ no nonempty product of which is a square, so [M : ℚ] = 2ⁿ; this is the field-theoretic half of the maximality of the genus field, whose arithmetic half — matching the aᵢ to prime discriminants — comes next (Cox, *Primes of the Form x² + ny²*, §6.A).

name: The half-disc residue theorem with enclosed poles
text: the generalized winding number of the boundary of the upper half-disc of radius R is 1 at every point inside it, ½ at the origin and 0 outside, so for f holomorphic off a finite set {0} ∪ S with at worst simple poles there and S in the open half-disc, the Cauchy principal value of ∮ f along that boundary is 2πi Σ_(s ∈ S) Res_s f + πi Res₀ f, the pole on the contour counting half; the version along the real diameter with the arc subtracted is the form real improper integrals consume (Henrici, *Applied and Computational Complex Analysis* I, Thm 4.8f).

name: Cartier divisors on an integral scheme
text: the sheaf 𝒦_X^×/𝒪_X^×, formed as a cokernel in sheaves of abelian groups rather than as a quotient of global sections, and its group of global sections Cartier(X) with the principal divisor map K(X)^× → Cartier(X); 𝒪_X(D) and the dictionary with line bundles are the next steps (Stacks 02AR; Hartshorne II.6).

name: The x − T map of an elliptic curve
text: for E: y² = f(x) over a field K of characteristic ≠ 2, with A = K[X]/(f) and T the class of X, the map E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² sending (x, y) to the square class of x − T (corrected at the 2-torsion, where x − T is a zero divisor) is a group homomorphism, because the classes of three collinear points multiply to 1; that its kernel is 2E(K), the descent computing E(K)/2E(K), is the next step (ported from Michael Stoll's *EllipticCurves*; cf. Silverman, *The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, X.1).

name: The Lie functor on morphisms
text: a smooth homomorphism φ of finite-dimensional real Lie groups induces a Lie algebra homomorphism Lie(φ) on left-invariant derivations, its differential at the identity, with Lie(id) = id, Lie(ψ ∘ φ) = Lie(ψ) ∘ Lie(φ) and φ(exp X) = exp(Lie(φ) X) (Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, ch. 3).

name: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every finite-dimensional module over a Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form is a direct sum of irreducible submodules, every Lie submodule having a complement (Humphreys, GTM 9, §6.3).

name: Irreducible highest weight modules are finite-dimensional exactly at dominant integral weights
text: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, an irreducible module over a Killing-semisimple Lie algebra generated by a highest weight vector of weight λ is finite-dimensional if and only if λ is dominant integral (Humphreys, GTM 9, §21.2).

name: The Clebsch–Gordan rule for sl₂
text: in characteristic zero, V(m) ⊗ V(n) is the direct sum of explicit submodules isomorphic to V(m + n − 2k), 0 ≤ k ≤ min(m, n) (Fulton–Harris §11.2).

name: Strong Kantorovich duality on compact spaces
text: for a continuous nonnegative cost on compact pseudometric spaces and probability measures μ, ν, inf_π ∫ c dπ over couplings equals the supremum of ∫φ dμ + ∫ψ dν over continuous (equally, integrable) potentials with φ(x) + ψ(y) ≤ c(x, y), extending the finite-space duality of 25 August (Villani, *Topics in Optimal Transportation*, Thm 1.3); attainment of the supremum is not claimed.

name: Frobenius–Schur indicator 1 means realizable over ℝ
text: an irreducible complex representation of a finite group has ν₂ = 1 exactly when it is the complexification of a real representation; the new half builds the real structure from an invariant symmetric and an invariant Hermitian form, completing the trichotomy of 8 August (Serre, *Linear Representations of Finite Groups*, §13.2).

name: Finite covering spaces form a Galois category
text: over a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base, the covering spaces with finite fibres form a Galois category (SGA 1) with the fibre over a basepoint as fibre functor.

name: The valence formula at general level
text: for a nonzero weight-k modular form on a finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ), Σ_P (2/|Stab_Γ P|)·ord_P f + Σ_c ord_c f = k·[SL₂(ℤ):Γ]/12, the cusp sum over the ⟨T⟩-orbits on SL₂(ℤ)/Γ with each order read in its own width; the level-one case was announced on 14 August (Shimura, Thm 2.20).

name: The Selmer group K(S, n) is finite, via its fundamental exact sequence
text: for a Dedekind domain with fraction field K and a set S of primes, 1 → 𝒪_S^×/(𝒪_S^×)ⁿ → K(S, n) → Cl_S[n] → 1 is exact, so K(S, n) is finite when Cl_S is finite and 𝒪_S^× is finitely generated, in particular for a number field and finite S — the three TODOs of Mathlib's `SelmerGroup.lean`; extended to finite étale algebras in TauCeti#4610 (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).

name: The Hecke ring of Γ₀(N) is commutative
text: the Atkin–Lehner anti-involution fixes every double coset Γ₀(N)xΓ₀(N), x ∈ Δ₀(N), so Shimura's criterion of 4 August makes R(Γ₀(N), Δ₀(N)) commutative, and the composite T_n = ∏_p T_{p^{v_p(n)}} satisfies T_{mn} = T_m T_n for coprime m, n (TauCeti#4720); the abstract Hecke ring is being upstreamed (mathlib4#41251, mathlib4#41277) (Shimura §3.3).

name: The kernel of the x − T map is 2E(K)
text: for E: y² = f(x) over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, the map μ : E(K) → A^×/(A^×)² announced yesterday has kernel exactly 2E(K), so E(K)/2E(K) embeds in the square classes of A = K[X]/(f) — the injectivity half of 2-descent (Silverman, AEC X.1).

name: The integral closure of a Dedekind domain is Dedekind, with no separability
text: for a Dedekind domain A and any finite extension L of its fraction field, the integral closure of A in L is Dedekind; Mathlib has this for separable L/K, and the Krull–Akizuki theorem of 25 August removes the separability, which now covers inseparable isogenies of elliptic curves (Bourbaki, *Commutative Algebra*, VII §2.5).

name: Deligne's bigrading is an internal direct sum
text: for a mixed Hodge structure the subspaces I^{p,q} of 24 August are independent and span the complexification, with (W_k)_ℂ = ⊕_{p+q ≤ k} I^{p,q}; recovery of F and the conjugation symmetry remain (Deligne, *Théorie de Hodge II*, 1.2.8).

name: The principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q) is irreducible exactly off the diagonal
text: Ind_B^{GL₂}(α ⊗ β) is irreducible if and only if α ≠ β; and the Steinberg character takes the values q, 1, 0, −1 on central, split semisimple, non-semisimple and elliptic elements (TauCeti#4732) (Fulton–Harris §5.2).

name: The spin representation is irreducible in odd dimension
text: for a polarised quadratic space of dimension 2l + 1 over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ 2, the even Clifford algebra is all of End(⋀W), so the spin representation is irreducible — the type B companion of the half-spin dichotomy of 21 August (Fulton–Harris §20.2).

name: The excursions of a recurrent Markov chain are i.i.d.
text: for a Markov kernel on a countable state space and a state a₀ returned to infinitely often almost surely, the successive excursions from a₀ are i.i.d., and the chain is the image of the infinite product of the excursion law under concatenation (Norris, *Markov Chains*, Ch. 1).

name: Maximal integral curves and the escape lemma
text: a C¹ vector field on a boundaryless manifold has through each point a maximal integral curve on an open interval, and at a finite endpoint the curve has no cluster point, so it leaves every compact set; hence every C¹ field on a compact manifold is complete (Lee, *Introduction to Smooth Manifolds*, 9.16, 9.19).

name: The representation ring
text: R(G), the split Grothendieck ring of FDRep k G under ⊕ and ⊗, with the character homomorphism R(G) → (G → k) whose image is exactly the virtual characters; injectivity is a later step (Serre, §9.1).

name: The invariant differential of an elliptic curve
text: ω = dx/(2y + a₁x + a₃) in the Kähler differentials Ω_{K(E)/F} of the function field, with ω ≠ 0 in every characteristic; that div ω = 0 is not yet proved (Silverman, AEC III.1).

name: The weak Mordell–Weil theorem
text: for an elliptic curve y² = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆ over the fraction field K of a Dedekind domain in characteristic ≠ 2, the subgroup 2E(K) has finite index in E(K), provided that for each irreducible factor p of the cubic the ring of integers of K[X]/(p) has finite class group and finitely generated unit group, as it does over a number field; proved by explicit 2-descent through the étale algebra K[X]/(f), adapting Michael Stoll's Lean development, and it is the finiteness that the descent argument for the Mordell–Weil theorem itself consumes (Silverman, AEC VIII.1).

name: The Fréchet–Kolmogorov compactness criterion in Lᵖ
text: for 1 ≤ p < ∞, on a proper normed abelian group with Haar measure and with values in a finite-dimensional real space, a family of Lᵖ functions that is bounded in Lᵖ, has translation increments ‖f(· + h) − f‖ₚ uniformly small as h → 0, and is uniformly tight is totally bounded, hence relatively compact; proved through Arzelà–Ascoli applied to ball averages, and it is the input Rellich–Kondrachov needs (Brezis, Thm 4.26).

name: Analytic sets are universally measurable
text: every analytic subset of a Polish space is measurable for the completion of every s-finite Borel measure (Lusin; Kechris, Classical Descriptive Set Theory, Thm 21.10), and hence the strict sublevel sets of a Borel c-transform in optimal transport are analytic, which makes c-transforms measurable in every finite-measure completion.

name: Strong approximation for algebraic function fields
text: for a function field F/k with exact constant field, a proper subset S of its places, finitely many P₁, …, Pᵣ ∈ S, targets fᵢ ∈ F and integers rᵢ, a single x ∈ F has ord(x − fᵢ) = rᵢ at every Pᵢ and is regular at every other place of S (Stichtenoth, Thm 1.6.5); proved from Riemann's theorem through the repartition space, in the form Goppa-code applications use.

name: The inflation–restriction exact sequence for continuous cohomology
text: for any topological group G, normal subgroup N and topological G-module M, the sequence 0 → H¹(G/N, Mᴺ) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M) of explicit continuous-cochain cohomology is exact (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.7)); Mathlib has the discrete-group version for Rep k G.

name: Shapiro's lemma for continuous cohomology in degrees 0 and 1
text: for a profinite group G, a closed subgroup U and a discrete U-module A, evaluation at 1 induces H⁰(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H⁰(U, A) and H¹(G, Coindᴳ A) ≅ H¹(U, A), the inverse built from a continuous section of G → G/U (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg (1.6.4)); degree 2 is not yet covered, and Mathlib has the discrete-group statement.

name: Faithfulness of the Lie functor on connected Lie groups
text: two smooth homomorphisms out of a preconnected finite-dimensional real Lie group that induce the same map of Lie algebras are equal, by naturality of the exponential map and its local inverse near the identity (Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, Ch. 20).

name: The Weil differentials of a function field form a one-dimensional space over it
text: for F/k with exact constant field, the Weil differentials Ω (the k-linear forms on the repartition space vanishing on some A(D) + F, with F acting by (f·ω)(a) = ω(f a)) satisfy dim_k Ω(D) = i(D), the index of specialty, and dim_F Ω = 1 (Stichtenoth, Lemma 1.5.7 and Prop. 1.5.9); the canonical divisor, duality and Riemann–Roch itself are the remaining steps.

name: The Kähler differentials of a function field are one-dimensional
text: if x is a separating element of F/k (x transcendental over k and F separable over k(x)), then Ω[F/k] is a one-dimensional F-vector space with basis dx, and y ↦ dy/dx is a k-derivation of F with dy = (dy/dx)·dx (Stichtenoth §IV.1), obtained from formally étale base change of Kähler differentials along k(x) → F.

name: The affine simply-laced Cartan form is positive semidefinite with radical spanned by the marks
text: for Ãₙ, D̃ₙ, Ẽ₆, Ẽ₇, Ẽ₈ the symmetrized Cartan form is positive semidefinite and its radical is exactly the line ℝδ spanned by the marks (Kac, Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras, Ch. 4), and deleting the affine node leaves the finite Cartan matrix of type Aₙ, Dₙ, E₆, E₇, E₈ in Bourbaki's numbering.

name: The weights of the spin representation
